I recommend that couples upgrade to RED Level (make sure you do it once you get there and not beforehand). A great place to relax. The Red Level experience was great, you have your own private pool and bed berths by the beach. Definitely recommended.

reviews.author: Elizabeth H
reviews.title: Awesome trip :)
reviews.text:
Me and my boyfriend just got back from this hotel yesterday. We were there for 6 nights. 

The goods: 

The hotel was really nice, clean and well maintenance.  The services we received were mostly good. Some of the waiters were really nice and attentive but some other ones weren't so much. So in terms of the service I would say it's a hit or miss. The staff speaks little English. 

As for the food, they offered many choices of restaurants that you can choose from. Good overall. My favorite restaurant was Vento. 

We did enjoy the nightly shows. Also the bartender Enrique Diaz was a amazing. He taught us how to  make our rainbow shots and they were goooood. Also Brenda the chef was really helpful during our guacamole class along with Karla, the friendly translator girl. 

The bads: 

1. We did have one complain about the Ecotour activity. The meeting point was really hard to find and none of the staff we approached in the meeting area knew where it is, some even said it's not on today when we just made our reservation that morning. The meeting point was really confusing and by the time we figured out where it shoudl be we were already 25 mins late,, needless to say we missed the acitivity and was really frustrated with the whole thing. 

2. Another thing we had to complain about was the concierge service - the girl name Rosa. She approached us on our arrival and took a long 30 mins to try to sell us extra service at the hotel when we were really tired and all we wanted was a key to our room and to rest after our long flight. We felt she wasted our time and she did pressure us into booking the next day "VIP tour of the hotel" to try to sell us more packages. We later called the ception that night to cancel the next 8.30am meetign with her for the tour as we weren't really interested, and the only reason we signed up cos we felt pressure and she had our room key. Despite that Rosa's manager felt the need to call us early next morning at 8.30am - when we were still asleep after the previous day long flight -  to ask us why we weren't coming and if he could "offer us some other packages instead". This was extremely annoying. We avoided Rosa and other concierge services for the rest of our trip as we find it more stressful.

reviews.author: Jennel M
reviews.title: Phenomenal all-inclusive experience!
reviews.text:
What a wonderfully relaxing experience! This was our first all inclusive trip, and it will be difficult to top it in the future! Great food! We started each day with egg white omelets (you can ask for egg white at the omelet station). Also, we would have a fresh juice made with whatever fruits and veggies we wanted! So refreshing! Our favorite dinner restaurant ended up being Fuego. Make sure you make reservations the day before with the concierge! We had a great experience with Erick de la Cruz at the pool bar - always willing to give great service and makes the BEST margarita on the resort ;) Thank you Erick! You made our first and last margarita of our trip! On our last night we upgraded to oceanfront view with a hot tub on the balcony - so worth it. For excursion we went to XPLOR near Playa Del Carmen. Highly recommended as well! We went zip lining, cave swimming, cave rafting, and ATV'd through the jungle all for 1 price :) Overall, Paradisus is a great location, great views, and great service! Thank you staff at Paradisus for making our experience a wonderful one!

The only thing I was surprised with is the lack of Mexican food...haha...I though there would be beans, guac, and salsa & chips every chance I got...not so much!!

reviews.author: Atl-TravelJunkie
reviews.title: Amazing hotel with a few gotchas
reviews.text:
I stayed at the Paradisus Cancun twice in the past few months.  Both times we upgraded to get ocean view rooms (definitely worth the money).  My first visit was for a long weekend getaway in October.  The property is absolutely gorgeous with a great beach and beautiful pools.  The hotel lobby is also beautiful.  With the decor, the hotel has a bit of a spa-like feel.   I liked the hotel so much that I returned for a 4 day trip in mid December.

PROS:
- Excellent service - great staff
- Beautiful property
- Very good food in the specialty restaurants, the main buffet is good but not great
- Nice large balcony's (but they seem to only come with one chair)
- Comfortable rooms
- Beach chairs are well spaced out, not on top of each other as happens in some resorts

CONS:
- The "personal concierge" is just basically a glorified sales person.  They will help you book your sightseeing trips (which is fine) but they will also attempt to get you to go on a Melia Club timeshare presentation.  On my second trip - the concierge lied to me about this (more below).

- The resort also has a conference center - during our second trip there was a conference including 1700 realtors that completely changed the feel of the resort from a laid back tropical paradise to more of a "Tony Robbins meets an adult spring break" vibe. There was no indication when we made the reservation that there would such a large group at the hotel.

THE GOTCHA
The Club Melia "Get a Free Trip promotion" is a COMPLETE SCAM.  For the record, I never do time presentations, I haven't been to one in over 15 years.  On my first trip, even though my "concierge" was doing a relative hard sell, I turned it down.  On my second trip, the concierge pointed out that I was staying for 3 nights.  He stated that if I had done the presentation, I could have been using a free 3 night certificate and suggested I do the presentation so that I could try one of the other Paradisus resorts.  I still resisted stated that there is always a catch.  We went back and forth for a while where I asked several specific questions he assured my that there were no hidden fees (boldface lie) just a $50 registration fee.   Since I am a big fan of the two Melia hotels that i have visited, I broke my rules and agreed to go to the 90 minute presentation to get a free ($50) 3 night stay.  THE CATCH: after the presentation when they game me the certificate, they stated that the hotel room is free for three nights but you must pay an all inclusive fee each night (which turns out to be at least $160 night making the "free" trip cost over $500 not $50).  I pointed out to them that this was in direct conflict from what I was told by the concierge. To which they pointed out was written clearly in the fine print of the document (which I did not have access to until after I wasted 90 minutes in the presentation).  I pointed out that I had asked several direct questions about the fees before booking the presentation and after complaining to management they gave me a free massage if I would sign the acceptance of the travel certificate.  The moral of the story: DO NOT DO A MELIA CLUB PRESENTATION.  The "free" trip is not free and has a series of restrictions.  You can do better booking a trip with hotel and air combined on Orbitz or Expedia.  

The sleazy timeshare pushing is a real negative for what otherwise appears to be a high end luxury hotel.

IN SUMMARY:
My first trip to the Paradisus in October was amazing.  I travel frequently and rarely return to the same property, however this was so nice that I went back.

My second trip to the Paradisus in December was still nice, but somewhat disappointing.  Two days before the large group arrived they began building a huge stage in the middle of the beach and putting large signage all over the property.  When the realtors arrived they had an event that complete took over the pool area. The zen feel that I enjoyed so much the first time was completely lost.

If there is a way to check that there are no large groups at the same time as your trip I would highly recommend the property.

reviews.author: Trucker13
reviews.title: Paradisus Cancun hits it out of the park again.
reviews.text:
My wife and I returned from the Paradisus a couple of weeks ago, and it was fabulous again. There were a couple of minor changes since Feb 2013. It felt like coming home as soon as I walked through the door. The great memories came rushing back.

We again were on the seventh floor, main tower 3. This time ocean view, and it was gorgeous, room 3704. People keep complaining about the noise in tower 3. Not sure what they are talking about. After 8:30-9:00 pm, it's not noisy, other than doors closing, or people walking by.

Again, the food was delicious, but even better than I remembered. There was a couple of hick-ups in the service, but overall still excellent. Everything from my last review of the Paradisus still stands. 

Props to Brenda, the hostess at the Market Grill. On our last night there, she was the hostess at Vento, and she remembered us. She sees hundreds of people a day, and remembered our name. Impressive. There are too many names to remember, and though the resort was near capacity, it was still a fantastic vacation. 

One thing though. I'm not certain small children should be allowed to sit at the swim up bar. 

I recommend this resort to everyone. Fantastic.

reviews.author: riz513ca
reviews.title: Great service and grounds but...
reviews.text:
We decided on the Paradisus for a 9 night stay leaving out of Vancouver with WestJet Vacations. Total cost per person was approximately $2400 with a hotel stay over in Calgary while en-route.

The hotel itself was built in the early 90's and consists of 5 pyramids. Pyramid 3 is the center hub with all the night life and restaurants. We stayed in Pyramid 1 following the recommendations of other travellers for some peace and quiet. Pyramid 5 on the other end appeared to be where those who opted for the Royal Service resided. 

We were picked up by a shuttle which was quite convenient and dropped off at the hotel. Check in was fine with a welcome cocktail of our choice offered. Definitely a nice start. 

The Room - We had an ocean view junior suite with a large balcony and small hot tub on the outer deck. The room was spacious but dated. All the furniture was well worn and could have benefited from replacement. The bed was slanted on both sides which had us rolling towards the edges when we slept. Our final two nights involved a water leak coming from the floor above us that ran down through the light fixture in our bathroom. It made for quite a mess as the water would collect in the suspended ceiling and then drip down all over the floor. 

Staff did what they could and offered us a room change but given the late hour, the fact that it eventually tapered off and we only had one more night before departure, we decided to stick it out. Second night was a bit wetter and we were told that the water had to do with a leak in the upper suites shower. I think we may have taken them up on the room change had we known the problem wasn't fixed. Regardless, the staff were great and very apologetic. They supplied us with extra towels to mop up and all was good. 

The Timeshare Pitch - We were prepared for this and know it's very common. We were offered a free massage, a half price tour and a bottle of tequila to attend (never did get the tequila tho). We toured the property and were informed of the various properties around the world that are part of Melia resorts. It was informative but not nearly enough to motivate us to make a decision right then whether or not we wanted to spend $50,000 without doing any research on our own. We asked for a few days to look into things ourselves prior to making a decision but that's not how it's done. 

The Food - Paradisus has multiple a la carte restaurants. We visited them all. Again service was excellent but the food, at least for us, was simply average. We noted that with the exception of the buffet, all food was served in small portions so consider ordering a bit more than you normally would to share. Food was readily available either by dining within the hotel or ordering room service. 

The Pools and Beach - Beautiful pools that were well maintained. At time it was a bit difficult to get a seat as there was a common practice of people staking out their territory in the morning and then not returning until late morning or early afternoon to take up their seats. It was posted that belongings left for longer than 30 minutes would be removed but I'd imagine this would be difficult to enforce. With a little footwork though, you will be able to find a spot either by the pools or beach. Again, we found the service very good. One thing we noticed about the beach was that it was windy and the water quite rough. It had been red flagged for swimming a number of times. I'm not sure if this is characteristic to this side of the island or if it simply was the time we were there but we didn't experience even one day where the water was calm and the winds weren't heavy. 

The Final Say - Overall and almost without exception, the service was excellent. The staff were kind and cordial and very accommodating. The pool and beach were beautiful and appearance and decoration of the hotel in the evening was beautiful. Unfortunately for us, the room quality and food fell short. In retrospect, the price paid for the package just didn't seem to be a good deal. At $255 per person per night, I'd consider simply getting a room at one of the many hotels up and down the strip and spending a bit more time exploring and dining out.

reviews.author: Renee W
reviews.title: Nice Hotel
reviews.text: Great location and great rooms! Beds were very comfortable.  Property is nicely kept and staff is very friendly. Mini bar was always fully stocked with a variety of items. Swim up bar staff was awesome.  Enrique was one of the bartenders at the swim up bar.  He was great!  They had some kind of activity at the pool daily.  We would stay here again!

reviews.author: Chris R
reviews.title: Loved it
reviews.text: I stayed at Paradisus for a business conference for a week and I can say my experience was absolutely great. My room had an excellent beachfront view with balcony, it was cozy and clean. I also loved the all-inclusive especially since the food at the restaurants was amazing. This was my first stay at a Melia Hotel, but I was pleasantly impressed. My only regret is that I'm only wishing I could have stayed longer after the conference was over! :)

reviews.author: Lisa H
reviews.title: EXCELLENT
reviews.text:
The Hotel Paradisus Cancun was EXCELLENT. Special mentions go to: Salvador in the bar near the Japanese restaurant; Roberto in the Japanese restaurant; Francisco who served us very well at the pool bar, and Ediel who worked at the pool bar too, and finally Ivan our butler. Very courteous, very polite, they all made our holiday an experience to remember.

The only negative I had out of the whole holiday was going to get breakfast in the Royal Service area on the day before we left. I was 'served' by two people who were chatting together the whole time (even whilst 'serving' me). She was called Karina, I did not manage to see his name. They probably need a bit more training. However they were the only negative experience and should not detract from the overall superb experience at this hotel. Definitely want to return.

reviews.author: Nidia L
reviews.title: Excellent hotel in Cancun
reviews.text: Almost everything was perfect for us: Delicious food,beverages and coffee,room service on time, excellent attitude and attention from: Fabrizzio in oriental restaurant, Humberto in Market grill, Sofonia in the beach. Breakfast in Naos very fresh, delicious and a lot options to choose. Bad thing: Fuego restaurant (Little portions and bad service)

reviews.author: 156happytraveller
reviews.title: Happy traveler
reviews.text: Overall, I had a great experience with the resort. I would recommend the Royal services for guest to enjoy. Management provides you with a butler who is at your service throughout the duration of your stay. Our butler (Hervik) was outstanding. He did over and beyond than what was expected. I enjoyed the mini bar. The mini bar was replenished everyday with coke products, native juices, and chocolate (mms). The resorts grounds were majestic. The resort was kept very clean. I have no complaints regarding the room or the resort grounds. A few staff members that stood out as distinguished members of the resorts. I really enjoyed Hervik (The Bulter) who not only provided exceptional service but made me and my wife feel at ease. Yuribe the massage therapist was very professional. The massage was very nice. I enjoyed the steam room and huge jacuzzi.  Roberto at IBano provided great service. Ibano was probably my favorite restaurant. Jose the outside bally bed concierge was very helpful. Overall the food was good. I enjoyed the variety. I wished the resort would have had food available 24 hours and also play more update club music at the red lounge

reviews.author: Cooki
reviews.title: Refuse to stay at any other Cancun resort!
reviews.text:
This resort is beautiful inside and out! The property is modern with a large section of beach. I have read most of the negative reviews on here, and while a few people may have run into some bad luck during their stay, others just seem to be extra picky and not understanding at all. I stayed at Paradisus three times in 2014 and am booked for another stay in March 2015. Like the title says, I won't even bother visiting Cancun if I can't get a room at Paradisus. 
    I chose the Royal Service option each time, and although you'll cough up extra dough for it, shouldn't your vacation be the best that it can be?? If you can afford it, I say splurge, it's worth it!
    I'm picky, not so much as to complain about a crooked outlet or curtains blocking too much sunlight in the rooms (I think that's their purpose) like I've read on here, but when it comes to the cleanliness of a hotel's common areas and it's rooms I definitely am since I worked as a hotel housekeeper in high school. So I know first hand how careless and lazy some hotel staff can be with their work. But the common areas at Paradisus are spectacular, there are staff constantly cleaning, and more importantly so are the rooms. I usually bring my own blanket when I travel and remove the one on the bed because I know for a fact most hotels don't wash the blankets and bedspreads between guests. But at Paradisus the comforter is tucked between two sheets that do get changed daily so I felt very comfortable using it. 
    I can't speak on the experience of other options, but Royal Service provides the ultimate convenience. Royal Service is for adults 18 and over only and the rooms are located in the fifth pyramid, so you are guaranteed not to hear little kids screaming through the halls or the music from the lounge and other activity associated with the other pyramids. I was told that Paradisus does not permit spring breakers to stay at the resort, which is a plus. I'm not sure how they regulate that, but it's an inviting concept. Royal Service guests have the pleasure of enjoying a pool, food and drink service and a section of beach all to themselves, again nobody under 18 permitted in those areas. A server will pass through the beach and pool areas every 10-15 minutes to take your food and drink orders and serve them to you while you soak up the sun. 
   Every item in the room's mini bar is included (no extra cost) and is replenished daily. If you prefer that your mini bar be stock with more of a certain item than others they will accommodate you. They even have a selection of alcohol that they will bring bottles of to your room if requested. The Royal Service atrium provides snacks, finger foods, and desserts during certain times of the day along with a help yourself bar of premium alcohol, all of which you can bring back to your room or enjoy right there. 
    At check in you are given a glass of sparkling wine and assigned a butler and a cell phone to contact him at any time. Request Sergio, he's the best! Any time I asked Sergio to bring something to my room he brought it in a timely manner or had someone else bring it. He never left us waiting unacceptable amounts of time. He's very nice and professional. He took care of all our reservation requests for restaurants and Bali beds, we never had any trouble. The Bali beds are no extra cost with Royal Service. And on our last full day Sergio arranged our airport transportation and printed out our boarding passes and brought them to us on the beach. 
    I'm a foodie at heart, I love to eat! The food at Paradisus is very good. As with any establishment not every item may be to your liking, but I had a hard time finding items I did not enjoy. The omelet station at the buffet and the Asian restaurant are my favs. I stayed at Grand Oasis my first two trips to Cancun, and trust me, the food at Paradisus would win awards compared to that "food". 
     Not everything went well during my stays, not to any fault of the staff, but our own. My friend was a bit hungover one morning and while at breakfast in the market grill buffet she passed out on her way to the restroom. It was unbelievable how many staff members came to her rescue. It was like they came out of nowhere even before she hit the ground! The medical staff took her blood pressure and were very caring. I had my own drunken moment at dinner. The wait staff noticed that I wasn't feeling well, I couldn't even sit up at the table, and they offered to bring me a wheel chair back to my room. And they even sent the food we already ordered to our room, which was unexpected. Well, we learned to control our drinking, but if you find yourself in a bind the staff and medical personnel are very attentive and compassionate. 
    Some people have complained about the "stink" in the lobby as being overwhelming. Well, I love the AROMA, I think it's lavender, and I can't wait to smell it again every time I leave. Most confusing are the complaints about the staff not being able to speak English. Well, you are in a Spanish speaking country, THEIR country. I say to those people , maybe you should learn Spanish. But anyway, the only staff I encountered who didn't speak English were some of the housekeepers and kitchen workers, I was still able to use my high school Spanish and get my point across. But all the staff whose purpose it is to assist and interact with guests speak English. Some people have griped that they arrived in the morning and had to wait hours for their room to be ready. Well, as with just about every hotel, check in time is at 3pm, it's stated on all booking websites. So unless you don't mind waiting for a ready room, I recommend you book your flight to arrive about noon if possible. By the time you collect your baggage, pass through customs, meet your transportation and travel to the resort it will be check in time or close to it. Others have complained that the common areas, especially the main lobby/atrium lacks AC leaving it hot and stuffy. You should understand that they may have the AC on, but with the main entrance doors, as well as the doors leading to the beach in the back constantly opening it makes sense that the AC wouldn't make much of a difference. But it would be understandable if they don't run the AC at all in those areas, it's just a waste. As long as the restaurants and my room is comfortable I'm happy! 
   The only complaint that I have is that the Wi-Fi signal in the rooms is very very weak. If I hang my phone on the room door's knob MAYBE  I can catch a signal, but usually I have to step into the hallway for a good signal. I would love to used my phone or tablet comfortably sitting in my room or even on the balcony. But throughout the common areas and even at the pool and beach area I received a signal. 
   I don't truly believe that tips are included in the package price, if they are, it's miniscule. If you receive great service as I always have during my stays please tip well, they deserve it.

reviews.author: KelseyLynnae
reviews.title: A Week in Paradise
reviews.text:
My mother and step-father have a time share with "Club Melia". They have been here multiple times over the years but this was the first trip with my husband and I, and my sister as well. The layout is very unique, but it is better to get a room farther from the main "pyramid", as there is less noise. We had a sweet on the third floor which was great. 

The food here is excellent! Every place we ate we enjoyed our meals - I am Dairy/Gluten intolerant, and they accommodated me as much as they could. There are many gluten free options at the Naos buffet and the Fuego restaurant. The Mango Gazpacho at Fuego is KILLER! Also the Bana Sushi restaurant is very yummy - lots of choices. Ask for Alberth Pech, he is an AWESOME waiter!!! Very kind and well versed in the food selection. If you want less of a crowd at the buffet, go right when it opens each time of the day.

Tips - Make sure you keep your towel card - it is $80.00 if you loose it OR the towel. You have to have your passport present to exchange money at the front desk. Although the shops are nice, it is cheaper to pay 20 pesos and hop on the bus at the bust stop (at the front of the resort - blue sign) and tell them you want to go to the Kuh Kla Khan mall. The mall has some major expensive retailers, and some cheaper stores mixed in. There is a nice new grocery store on the second floor where you can pretty much find anything you need - food or product. Cross to the other side of the street safely by the Liverpool store to hop on the bus in the other direction when heading back.

Children are welcome, but there is one kids area inside and a little pool area outside. There are  performances almost each night at the Avenue Bar on the 2nd floor, but there is NOT enough room. It is very tight- so if you want to see a show, get there early! All in all, if you go the all inclusive route you will really enjoy yourself. Take time to go on a trip (We did the Coba Go Native trip which was amazing!) You can book them at the hotel. Also bring change to tip not only your servers but the maids as well - they work SO hard and our rooms looked SO good every day! We had a great time! :) :)

reviews.author: Tristan S
reviews.title: Beautiful accommodation with inconsistent service and terrible operations management
reviews.text:
I stayed here for a full week with my wife and another couple. This was our first time staying in Mexico so I can only compare it to other international accommodation. We booked through RCI which the other couple had a membership in, so I cannot comment on the booking process except to say that the price was extremely inexpensive for the value we received. The room for a full week was less than $300 USD _total_ and the all-inclusive fee was $84 per person per night. We got that price by booking half a year ago before their price hike. I have heard that the all-inclusive fee is now around $200 for new bookings at this time of year, which in my opinion would be a very poor value.

First the good. The resort and beach are beautiful, assuming you don't mind some seaweed. The waves were complex, which made for great fun playing in the ocean, but it would not be good for people that want to actually swim, and there are no real lap pools. That was fine for us since we are not avid swimmers.

The buffet food quality was surprisingly good--probably the best I've had at a buffet (but I'm no buffet expert)--and the variety and quality of alcohol included in the all-inclusive plan was generous. There was also no push-back on quantity. If anything they had the opposite problem of occasionally overserving guests. (We ourselves had too much one afternoon and regretted it.)

We thoroughly enjoyed the trip, but there are a lot of things that the hotel could do better. Service was very inconsistent. Some servers and bartenders were eager to please, but many more tended to forget orders, disappear for long periods, etc. The table service at the buffet was particularly bumpy. We were never once seated at a table that was fully set-up. Tables were always missing something such as napkins or  coffee cups and sometimes even had dirty napkins. In one hilarious case we were seated at a table where every setting had two knives on the left and right and no other cutlery.

The main problem though was terrible operations management. The system for reserving the non-buffet restaurants shows it the most. Other than Blue Agave, all the non-buffet restaurants ostensibly require reservations, which can be made at most one day in advance and must be made either by phone or by physically going to a single desk in the center of the resort. This desk is supposed to be open from 9 to 5 and people line up before 9 to have first pick. The staff enter the reservations into a computer and issue a printed slip with the reservation details. At some point, someone transfers the information to paper reservation books at each restaurant. Obviously this is inherently error-prone, and one night we ended up with a printed slip that said 7:30 even though the restaurant was expecting us at 7:00.

In addition to the inherent ridiculousness of this process, on Wednesday no one showed up to staff the desk. It was over a half hour before someone in the know came by to inform everyone in line that the desk was not going to be open at all that day (information that was not communicated in advance anywhere AFAWCT). The hotel then placed a staff member at the desk to simply inform guests that showed up that the desk was closed! It was only at this point that we learned that the phone line to make reservations did not simply call that desk but rather went to a call center of some sort. However, calls we made were not picked up, and even the hotel concierge was unable to get through to anyone. We eventually managed to get reservations in late afternoon.

Strangely, the non-buffet restaurants were never visibly full, yet it was always hard to get reservations for the day and time that we wanted. Perhaps the reservation process is so frustrating that few people are willing to make the effort to cancel reservations that they no longer need. We did find that walk-ins are sometimes accepted (contrary to stated policy).

Another area of poor operations management is the cabanas/balinesas. They have an all-paper system for paid reservations charged to the room, yet there was much confusion about the price. One person told us $25 USD per cabana per day, one told us $20, and the actual bill at check-out was $10. On one occasion, we went to reserve beach cabanas for the next day and were told we could have cabana numbers 216 and 217. However, when we went to the beach the next day we discovered that cabanas 216 and 217 did not exist. Luckily there were still two cabanas available, although not adjacent.

This brings me to the poor maintenance of the beach cabanas. The beach cabanas (unlike the poolside cabanas) are open-sided structures with a fabric roof and fabric curtains that can be tied down to create a windbreaker, which works surprisingly well except when the curtains are torn or missing, which was almost always. Of the dozen or so beach cabanas, only a few had enough intact curtains to provide adequate wind protection, and when I asked the staff on one occasion for additional curtains they said they did not have any. To be clear, the poolside cabanas are a different design and were mostly out of the wind. Being at the same price, they were clearly preferable, and reservations for them tended to fill up more than one day in advance. I do recommend that you reserve at least a day in advance because there is a turn-up service that we didn't always get when we made a same-day cabana reservation. However, you would probably not be able to reserve anything before check-in. Even the spa was poorly set up to take reservations from outside the hotel. We looked in to booking spa services in advance and found that, although an online reservation form exists, the brochure of services and their prices is not posted anywhere.

Lastly I will mention check-out. It is 10 AM, which was a bit of a surprise given that check-in is 4 PM. My guess is they want to employ as few housekeeping staff as possible. But what ticked me off was that our bill was in pesos yet, without asking, they charged me in USD with a 3% currency conversion fee. When I asked about the presence of a USD amount on the receipt, the check-out agent said that that was just for my information and that the transaction would be in pesos. Only later when I read the fine print on the receipt did I see that that was untrue. It only cost me an extra $30, but it's the principle of the thing! If you know that your credit card gives you a fair currency conversion rate, I recommend that you insist at check-out to be charged in pesos.

So with so many problems, why 3 stars, you ask? Well, at the right price, all-you-can-eat-and-drink and a beautiful beach go a long way ...

reviews.author: Nick C
reviews.title: Christmas and New Year in Mexico
reviews.text:
We have just spent an excellent 12 days staying in the Paradisus in Cancun. We booked the Royal Service and it was well worth the additional costs, having your own butler and access to the adults only section and pool was great. The rooms were large, comfortable and exceptionally clean. The concierge team of Natalia and Karla could not do enough for us, from booking restaurants to arranging various outings. Our butler Hervik was excellent, nothing was ever too much trouble, he even arranged for champagne, chocolate and rose petals for a romantic evening. The pool concierge team of Alexander and Bernardo worked hard to ensure we had cabanas and chairs everyday.

The hotel has plenty of restaurants, which we were able to book tables most evenings, but a couple more bars would be an improvement. We were all inclusive with all the drinks being premium brands and a great selection of food.

Situated in the hotel district of Cancun, right on the beach, there was a good selection of activities and a small 9 hole golf course in front. With buses every couple of minutes into town a great place for a family break.

Highly recommended, we would book again.

reviews.author: diane s
reviews.title: Outstanding!
reviews.text: This hotel is outstanding in every way. The service is wonderful, the food is great. Our second visit and will go again. We especially enjoyed Francisco and Juan at the Avenue Bar. It is important to get up early to get chairs at the beach or pool.

reviews.author: senoralberto
reviews.title: Perfecto!
reviews.text:
This simply is a wonderful resort.  We stayed 12/28 to 1/4 (2 adults, 2 young children) and were treated incredibly well from our arrival through our departure.  

We did Family Concierge and stayed in building 1 which I recommend for families with young children, and our kids made great friends at the kids pool just outside building 1.

The beach is fantastic.  Great waves, a lifeguard, and they even clean the seaweed.  

The restaurants are great.  Juan @ Fuego made our anniversary even more special, the Brazilian steakhouse was really good and fun, Tempo is great tapas, the breakfast and dinner buffets have something for everyone and all of the restaurants are beautiful.  

The service throughout is wonderful...and sincere.  Charly our butler arranged for rose pedals throughout our room, around the tub filled with bubbles and leading into our room while we were at dinner for our anniversary.  He called us daily to see if we needed anything.  We were too busy having fun in the pool and ocean to hear his calls so he came to the beach and pool to find us. 

The hotel smells wonderful, the shows at night are very entertaining and my only regret is that we had to leave.

reviews.author: IreneZCPA
reviews.title: Average hotel in Cancun
reviews.text:
Pros: beautiful design of the hotel. 
Cons: old, not well cooked food, rooms, service.

I have been in this hotel on January,1-6. I am New-Yorker. I have been several times in Mexico and before I was living in Secrets hotels.
Paradisus made a mixed impression. From one point of view, it is fine. From another: it is outdated and overrated.
Check-in. Instead of being welcomed by converge, we have been sent to the front desk area which reminds fast-food place. Nobody told us anything about the hotel. No information was given. We had to explore this hotel on our own.
Room. It is really old and small. Nothing to talk about. Due to high season we didn't get any chairs on balcony.
Beach. You need to wake up really early to reserve you beach chair. Without it you are going to lay on sand and be ignore by waiters. They have VIP Royal area as well. For additional charge you will get service that you are expected to get any way from a good Mexican hotel. People here said that it is hard to get a chair at the beach but once I saw that outside Mexican man not guest came and paid some money to guys and got two chairs to enjoy the beach. Along with chairs he got drinks and towels while guests were laying on the sand.
Food. Seafood smells like antibiotics or some chemicals. Stake house Le Perla is a joke. Do not go there under any circumstances. Food was average and really nothing to talk about. 
Service. I know it is a high season, but still service was not Mexican level. 

Summary. Comparing with Secrets this hotel is 3+ stars. It doesn't worth money they ask for. The only good thing is a beach, but beach is everywhere the same. I would prefer to stay away from this place.

reviews.author: mca2012
reviews.title: Slightly Disappointed
reviews.text:
La Perla restaurant - bad service, impolite staff and disgusting cold leftover from the day before food. I am not one to voice my opinion openly in a restaurant but this time wow.

The rest of our stay was as good as you get in an All Inclusive. The lack of management overseeing the staff was the biggest downfall.

reviews.author: Staceyeliz02
reviews.title: Brilliant hotel - royal service excellent!
reviews.text:
Stayed at the paradisus in cancun for a week, we had the royal service which i would recommend - you get afew nice extras like the butler service ( can make reservations etc for you ) access to adults pool along with the lovely Bali beds & there is a lovely little restaurant you can have breakfast & lunch at rather than the Buffett which over looks the sea and is very nice! 
All the restaurants in the hotel were really nice and great food - it can get a little stuffy in the evening as there doesn't seem to be much air conditioning in the area where the restaurants are but not too bad. 
All the staff were friendly and helpful & rooms clean and nice. You do need to get sunbeds early as there didn't seem to be enough for everyone. In the evenings the hotel put a show on however there is no where enough space for this and no- where for people to watch the show, this seemed to be the only entertainment in the evening and finished quite early. 
The wifi in the hotel was ok - not so good by the pool sometimes didn't work at all!
Hotel was in good location as can get the bus for $1 and go shopping / clubs / bars etc 
Overall would recommend hotel had a great time!

reviews.author: DMF Rossi
reviews.title: New Year's week in Cancun
reviews.text: We went to Cancun, Mexico for New Years week! Paradisus is the place to stay! We got the Royal Service.. Well worth it! Juan our Butler was the best! The food and drinks never stopped! Food was delish! The beach there was awesome! I stayed at RIU Cancun 2 years ago, & the beach there is terrible! Love Paradisus! I'm going back!!

reviews.author: Wendy E
reviews.title: Paradisus Cancun
reviews.text:
Excellent winter vacation get away!  We visited during the early part of December 2014 and encountered some excellent customer service, especially in the dining area.  Jorge, Edgar dela Cruz, Joel and Edgar Gamboa were exceptional and deserve a HUGE thank you for making our stay superb  :0)

Wendy

reviews.author: M.e. S
reviews.title: Almost awesome...
reviews.text: This is a lovely hotel, the grounds are beautiful, the beach clean and large, and the staff is very friendly and helpful.  The food is actually very, VERY good for an all inclusive.  Although we went over the Christmas holiday and the place was booked, we never felt like it was over crowded.  Rooms are big, beds are comfy.  We stayed in the Royal Service which is worth it even if just for the location at the resort, private pool and beach.  Now the "almost" part...we found the butler service to be pretty nonexistent. He did help with our dinner reservations, that's about it.  There was no butler cell phone, no help in the room, no pillow menu, etc.  The pool cabanas are only available two nights of your stay and you cannot request the location of your cabana, you get whatever they assign.  But the round the clock food in the Royal service area was great, the pool service amazingly attentive, although the restaurant was a little slow.  But hey, we were on vacation.  We went to the Paradisus in DR last year, regular service..and the upgraded service this time, we felt was worth it..even if the butler didn't work out so well!  We would go back.

reviews.author: Nenako
reviews.title: Good stay, maybe a bit noisy
reviews.text:
I have stayed at the Paradisus Cancun from 25th Dec for four days with my husband and 2 years old son. 
First time in Cancun area. Stayed twice in Riviera maya (Iberostar Maya and Grand Sirenis).
I prefer Riviera Maya because the resorts are bigger, more to do. But Cancun was also nice because hotels are much closer to the airport and beach is cleaner and sandy. 
 
Room was a bit dated, but kept clear, good size, but the door was thin, so you could hear 
music/voices coming from outside of the room. And our room was in main building where they played music loud from 8pm to late night. It was noisy. Bed was comfortable. WIfi in the room was good/ok, but around pool area, it was hard to get signal.

Pool was very nice. One of the pool in front of the buffet restaurant was heated, which was great for my son. Other pools were colder, but swimmable for me. By the way, pools were deep, 1.8m most of the area. 
No kids slides. Cabanas can be booked for 50$/day, and I loved it. 
They had adult only pool, which I did not go in, but looked quiet and nice. 

Food was good. Buffet had good selection, one night they even had sushi at buffet.
I tried one of the asian food restaurant (by the way I am from Japan) and they were good. 
Not super great, but very good for all-inclusive resort. 

Over all great stay, maybe not family oriented resort, but staff were very kind to my super active boy.

reviews.author: belindah15
reviews.title: Royal Service all the way-except excessive incense burning.
reviews.text: Royal Service -4th trip-Great get-away for relaxing and being pampered; a place to run away and leave the world behind. The feel of a quaint escape, yet even when full; big enough to feel like we are the only folks they have to serve. Our butler, Sergio is the best! Not 5 Stars because this time was excessive incense burning and fragrance machine. Very hard for people with asthma or breathing issues. Couldn’t enjoy the indoors because of it. Noticed no one lingered inside as well. Planning trip #5, if this is now common practice-may have to look elsewhere. Otherwise- 5*

reviews.author: DovBaron
reviews.title: Royal Pool Service
reviews.text: Despite many disappointments with this property we have received some great pool service. Bernardo, (pool concierge) find this best spots and keeps everybody happy. Octavio, pool butler; outstanding prompt service, goes above & beyond

reviews.author: Alex_54321
reviews.title: Very good all inclusive resort
reviews.text:
We had a pleasure of staying at Paradisus Cancun for 9 nights over New Year's 2015

LOCATION: Paradisus Cancun is located right on the beach in Cancun's hotel zone, near the middle of its north-south stretch. At this distance from the city, both auto and pedestrian traffic along the Kukulkan boulevard is light, and any noticeable shopping is also a bit far away. There is no problem getting around hotel zone using public buses, the fare was 10.5 pesos one way, and buses coming very frequently. Venturing into the city, however, can be more complicated. One day, we decided to visit "Market 28" in Cancun. We got into the bus proudly showing "Market 28" on its windshield as one of its major stops. It turned out that the bus route doesn't go close to Market 28, one has to get off at Walmart stop and walk several blocks towards the market. We didn't know that and ended up getting a bus tour around poor section of the city. At the final stop, the driver explained to us where we should have been getting off, and on a return trip we successfully disembarked to visit both Market 28 and Walmart. The lesson: unless you are familiar with the place where you are going, tell about it to the driver beforehand. Drivers are speaking at least some English and are willing to help. Lesson #2: tequila at Walmart is cheaper that at Cancun airport's duty free shop.

The hotel itself is rather pretty, both inside and outside. It consists of five connected pyramids, with the central one, #3, also the biggest one and housing a huge atrium inside. One side of the hotel is facing Kukulkan boulevard and the lagoon. On that side, there is a sizable park with well-maintained lawns that is virtually empty at all times. You can meet and try to befriend some iguanas that enjoy sunny weather. On the other side of the hotel is the beach, and also the swimming pools. That's where most of the people hang out, and I wish that side was made bigger; iguanas could do well with a smaller lawns.

ROOMS: Rooms at the hotel are sizable and comfortable. They are not very new, but appear to be clean and well-maintained. There is a minibar in room with water, soft drinks and beer - all free for all-inclusive guests, even for the lowest-rung ones like us. The floor in the room is made of stone, and I would recommend getting slippers (the resort will get it for you for free, but you have to ask). All balconies have flowerbeds, which, in my opinion, is a brilliant way to provide privacy. Without flowerbeds, one up in the pyramid would have a full view of the balconies below. Also, rooms have TV (with most channels in Spanish), seating sofa, alarm clock, coffee machine, iron and ironing board, safe, bathtub, hair dryer, and, surprisingly, a book "Teachings of Buddha" instead of a customary Bible.

As we arrived much earlier than the regular check-in time of 3 PM, we were offered either a room right away, but with 2 beds, or wait until 3 PM and get another room with a king-sized bed. Also, we could switch from 2 beds room next day, if we liked. We took 2 beds room and were pleasantly surprised. Not by the beds, but with a view - it was a 7th floor oceanview room in the main pyramid, close to center. I decided that chances of getting anything better than that are almost nonexistent, so we stayed in that room for the whole vacation. I would definitely recommend getting an oceanview room. Other room's view could be much worse. Staying in main pyramid has its pros and cons. First, its taller that the others so you (potentially) can get better view. Second, it's close to all restaurants and activities - you need only a ride down in an elevator. On the other hand, the central atrium has good acoustics, and in the evening you can hear music from restaurants and bars below.

FOOD: Paradisus Cancun has a central buffet called NAOS, which is open for breakfast, lunch and dinner. It has the widest variety of foods and is the default dining option for guests. 90% of the time, you can gorge yourself with great food. One morning, I was trying to pour myself some coffee from a carafe that usually stay on tables. The stream was weak. I tilted the carafe more. Still weak. I inverted the carafe upside down. Still weak. Is it empty? No... A-ah, I've got it, the carafe lid needed just a li-itle nudge... Whoah! In an instant, the whole carafe of hot coffee filled my cup, the table in front of me and spilled on my hand and on the floor. Ok, I've got it now. First the lid, then the tilt... first the lid, then the tilt...

The resort also has a number of other restaurants that open for dinner, but one has to book a table on the previous day. This arrangement was not very convenient for us, because we explored Yucatan in "day in - day out" mode. This way, one day there was no point for us to book a dinner, because next day we expect to spend in Chichen-Itza. Next day we could not make any booking because we were out of the hotel. The day after the next, again, no point of booking because Xcaret trip is coming, and so on.

Still, we managed to visit a few dinner places:
Bana - sushi, Japanese food. Reasonably good, nice ambiance among the greenery at the bottom of main atrium. Thumbs up, but more for ambiance than for food;
Blue Agave - tasty tacos. Note, this resort is generally not pushing Mexican cuisine, so Blue Agave is one of only few places where you can enjoy it. Thumbs up;
La Perla - thumbs down. Limited menu, slow service and leathery steaks. Next evening I was having grilled meat at NAOS buffet which was heavenly good, and was wondering how is it possible that a restaurant which was positioning itself as a steakhouse was hands down beaten by a buffet. Truth to be told, though, you can't get full variety of grilled meat at NAOS every evening;
Market Grill - lot of grilled meat for almost any taste. Thumbs up.

POOL/BEACH: The hotel has a nice Caribbean beach with white sand that doesn't burn your feet. The sea was not as much hospitable during our stay - every day there was a strong breeze and "Jersey Shore" - type surf. Red flags, meaning "no swimming" were propped along the beach every day. But not all of them were always red - on better days, some of them were replaced with yellow ones, meaning "swim witch caution". Why only some? Apparently, some parts of the beach are more dangerous than the others. I could feel some strong lateral current in the water, so strong that I could not overcome it with my swimming when I tried. From more dangerous parts of the beach, lifeguards were pulling people out of the water with some regularity. But don't worry. The real dangers of staying at Paradisus are overeating and overdrinking.

The main pools lie between the beach and the building. They are comfortable for swimming and not very crowded, but too deep for children. Sunbeds around them (and down on the beach), unfortunately, are heavily contested. Many people would "reserve" them with a beach towel first thing in a morning. So, very often by 9 AM there were no free sunbeds left outside of Royal Service zone. Then, "evictions" start to happen, when towels are getting removed and sunbeds - "stolen". Some people return from a swim or a walk along the beach to find out that their sunbeds are gone. And some people never return for their towels, not even in the evening when hotel workers are collecting and folding the beds. I think getting upgraded to Royal Service makes sense just to avoid this whole sunbed hassle.

Bali beds on the beach are a whopping $100 a day, and they were mostly occupied.

STAFF: Housekeeping was a mixed bag. The staff was always caring and attentive, and whenever they did anything, they did it well. However, it was very typical for them to miss replenishing something - towels, bathroom rug, toiletries, tissues, coffee, water, etc. Maybe trying to compensate, they often did another round of housekeeping in the evening, asking if we needed anything. Waiting staff at the buffet was very nice and attentive, but also often busy.

ENTERTAINMENT: During the day, hotel has animation group working at the main pool, it's a good fun for children and adults both. In the evening, there is music inside at the Bana restaurant. Usually, it's a lady singing karaoke hits. She has a nice voice, but her renditions were so placid and passionless, so when recognizing some popular songs, I was wondering - "Is it really this song?" On two of the nights, I've seen a duet, a lady and a gentleman, singing the same, as well as other, more challenging songs. This duo was truly amazing. I don't know if they are a regular event at Paradisus, or they brought them only for holidays, but I appreciated their singing quite a lot.

INTERNET: Good thing - WiFi at the hotel is free, and signal is strong even of the beach. Bad thing - connection is often terrible. Between 12 AM -7 AM you can usually get stable page loading and even Skype calls, but at other times there might be nothing coming through, nothing at all. I guess hotel's internet is totally overwhelmed.

Pros: beach, food, service
Cons: crowdiness, WiFi

reviews.author: tyanger
reviews.title: Family of 4 _ 3 nights _ never left the resort
reviews.text:
Just got back yesterday from a 3 night stay at the Paradisus Cancun with my wife and 2 kids (11,9). We had not been back to Yucatan Peninsula since our stay at the Occidental Grand Xcaret 7 years ago, and it was a very pleasant surprise. This was a last minute vacation (booked 6 days before departure just to escape cold weather for a few days) so we  weren't really expecting anything extravagant.
--The first time we stepped through the main entrance into Pyramid 3 we were all impressed by the overall ambiance - much fancier than we were expecting. Check-in was smooth. The room (3412) was clean, with a decent view of the lagoon, and the balcony was large. The A/C was kind of loud and seemed to cycle frequently, but it kept the room cool. One night there was a performance of some kind in Pyramid 3, and while we could hear the music from our room everyone was able to sleep without difficulty.
 --We were unable make it to all the restaurants during this visit since we were only there 3 nights.  The ones we did try were very good. We arrived a little late on our first day, so after checking in and settling into the room it was already  about 10pm. Naos, the main buffet, closed at 11pm so we had a late dinner/snack and it was good - nothing fancy, just good with enough variety that everyone was happy. We also ate breakfast there every day - also good. We had dinner one night at the Market Grill where they serve meat on large skewers and slice the servings at your table. It's not absolutely on par with Fogo de Chao, but for an all-inclusive resort I would say it is very good. The last night we ate at Bana, the sushi place and again, while it's not on par with the best sushi places I've been too, considering I'm eating at an all-inclusive in Cancun I would also consider it very good. (The Mango Tangos were so good.) Be sure to make your dinner reservations early for the restaurants that require them - if possible on the day you arrive. I saw more than one irate group caught after 6pm unable to eat at the places they wanted when they wanted to.
 --The beach is a beach - moderate amount of seaweed(+/-). Surf was moderately rough, I'd guess 3 to 5 foot waves(+/-). There were generally enough covered tables and lounge chairs, but just barely(+/-). If you didn't hit the beach early enough you might not get one. Which brings up a pet peeve - many people 'stake out' lounge chairs and tables and then disappear for hours without using them(-). My kids liked to maximize beach time so we were pretty much done with breakfast and on the beach by around 8:30am. One day there was a group of 5 lounge chairs marked with a flip flop and a towel on each one near our table. No one showed up until almost 12pm to use them. This was not an isolated incident. I'm not dinging the resort, just venting about bad behavior. The servers were present and kept drinks coming if you wanted them(+). Very few beach vendors (+).
 --The pools are nice and clean(+). The long meandering one was colder, and I think the big rounder one was heated. Harder to find lounge chairs by the pool than the beach IMO - again with moderate number of ghost loungers(-).
 --One last minor quibble. In order to print our boarding passes on the last day we had to use the downstairs gift shop. The front desk did not offer this service, the gift shop charges 8 pesos per b&w copy, and they only take pesos or credit cards. I had to charge 32 pesos to get my boarding passes. Still worth it if you don't have to check in bags, but slightly annoying.
 --Overall, I'd say it is an excellent resort and if I plan another trip to Cancun I would not hesitate to stay here again.
TIPS:
1) Consider using a prepaid airport transfer service. We used entertainment-plus.net
2) Make dinner reservations early

reviews.author: Michael M
reviews.title: What a great vacation or meeting destination!!
reviews.text:
My wife and I visited the Paradisus Resort in Cancun, Mexico from 12/6/2014 to 12/14/2014. We signed up for their "Royal Service" and it was spectacular service!! We were there to attend a medical conference but stuck some extra days on before and after the meeting.

There are too many folks to thank and acknowledge but suffice it to say, we had a wonderful vacation holiday.

Some of the folks who stood out included:
Our Butler- Rodrigo
Our Pool side servers- Octavio, Rodgelio, Javier, and Francisco
Our Wine Somelier- Iran
Our Front Desk crew at Royal Service- Leticia, Flavio, Natalia, and Karla
The Resturant staff- Leonardo (Mole and Blue Agave Resturants); Rodio and Sonya.

Special thanks to the Chef from NACO buffet (I didnt get his name unfortunately). He prepared my freshly caught red snapper and trigger fish as I requested, "Mayan Style". My fisherman buddies, their wives and several other couples in our group enjoyed the meal that the chef prepared and some are still raving about it. It was the best red snapper I have ever eaten.

The rest of the food in the several resturants was also wonderful. I loved the Market Grill Rodizio and the Mole/ Blue Agave mexican resturants.  The food and beverages overall were high end and plentiful. 

We have stayed at all inclusive resorts before but this one was by far, the best we have experienced. The hotel is very spacious and comfortable. Our room faced the blue Caribbean Sea and was exquisite.

The management and resort staff have blended together well and have created a great team.

Best regards to my new familia at the Paradisus Cancun.
Mike Milner

reviews.author: malanks
reviews.title: Beautiful beach + delicous food!
reviews.text:
My friends and i went in December for a quick relaxing all-inclusive post Christmas trip. The hotel is massive, but VERY CLEAN (we even got towels 2X a day in the room) and the beach is also SUPER clean. We tried a few restaurants (Argentinian steak place -market grill was delicous; sushi restaurant in the hotel lobby was also super fresh; el fuego was also very good for latin fusion). The least favorite was Mole -- the salads are weird and bland, the service was good, but the food in the buffett was better.

all the bartenders were super friendly. Oscar and Salvador at the Sushi bar made amazing cocktails!

Its definitely worth buying a bottle on the beach and getting a cabana. Its very reasonable for all the services you get. Luis, Chewy and Ricardo were very attentive and made the day really enjoyable.

Its also definitely worth getting an ocean front room, the hotel is on the strip and if you face the front...there isnt a view (at least its nothing compared to the one of the ocean).

There is an adults only section...but we didnt check it out (as it was an extra $95/night pp).

The main reason i didnt give this resport 5 stars is at the check in/check out there is room for improvement. Our room wasnt ready until after 4pm (check in is at 3pm), and when we got there, we had a "hostess" sit with us for alsmot 45 min trying to sell us on some promotion that if we sign up now, we can have 2 adults, 2 kids stay free (we were a group of 3 females in our late twenties....). And they omitted telling us about the schedule of events/where to find it. At check out, it was mass chaos....instead of having multiple lines for each clerk....people were using it was one line and saying "well i was here longer". They should really streamline that a little better.

reviews.author: Sara B
reviews.title: Royal Service all the way!!!
reviews.text: Natalia at concierge is amazing!! We were so pampered.  Private pool and bar were the best.  Can't wait to return. The food was way above expectations also. Can't not day enough about this place.  It was so beautiful.

reviews.author: Abbikash
reviews.title: Almost perfect
reviews.text: The accommodations are excellent. We stayed in the royal service adults only side.  The rooms were good, beds comfy and clean with nice amenities.  The "personal butler" system is pretty worthless. We were never assigned one after being told he would be up with a bottle of wine for us. No one showed. We finally went and requested one the next day who had to be repeatedly reminded of what we had requested. He was still better than some of the stories we heard. Only restaurant that wasn't good was La Perla. The steak was paper thin, overcooked and leather so we left. Fitness center was excellent, best we've ever seen. Only complaint would be that for that busy time, there were more guests than people and we had to go reserve chairs at 630am. beach surf is rough and many people had to be rescued, so please be careful.

reviews.author: Kirsty B
reviews.title: Lovely stay but disappointed by Butler service.
reviews.text:
We stayed at the Paradisus for a week over New Years. Pulling up to the hotel we were impressed by the beautiful lobby area and friendly staff. 

Our check in procedure did take an exhaustingly long time with every check in seem to be taking forever. During the check in we upgraded to the Royal Service and we're so pleased we did. For other who are wondering, you can do this when you get to the hotel and don't need to do this when you book initially.

Our room was a 1 bedroom suite. It was nice but not as modern as I would've hoped. We were shown to our room by our designated butler who would be on hand for the duration of our stay. He showed us around the facilities of the room and said he would meet us at 8.30 to take us to the restaurant for dinner. Disappointingly he was late and so we left without him, not wanting to wait around for someone else on our own holiday. 

Unfortunately this was just the start of quite a bit of disappointment caused by our "butler". He booked us into several restaurants for the beginning of our stay and importantly we had requested a restaurant for new years eve. 

We found out the night before that he had not booked us anywhere for that night or the night of new years eve. This left us in quite a sticky position. We ended up eating out at a restaurant called Puerto Madero. It was brilliant and i'd recommend it if you're planning on dining out of the hotel resort at any point but it cause us quite a bit of faffing about during our stay trying to find somewhere to go. 

Apart from the above we were really happy to be at the Royal Service Adults only pool. The facilities were beautiful and it was so lovely to be able to watch the waves go by with a pina colada in hand! 

In general the staff were very friendly and helpful and the service elsewhere at the hotel was great. 

The food was tasty and you're in luck if you're a mexican lover because the tacos and guacamole were super. Our tip for breakfast is to go to the Palapa restaurant for royal service by the beach. We only really noticed it towards the end of our trip and the al a carte breakfasts there were fab!

Drinks choice was good. Wifi good. Make sure you reserve a bali bed round the pool, they were lovely. 

I'd definitely recommend the hotel if you stay in Royal Service and I will be returning to Cancun. We loved it.

reviews.author: Saraimari
reviews.title: No Regrets
reviews.text:
We just visited this piece of heaven on earth during the holidays, the week of New Year and were pleasantly surprised. Words cannot do justice to the experience, but I will try. The room was superior in decor, amenities and the best part was the ocean view and the Jacuzzi. The Jacuzzi was on the terrace which was perfect. Our room had rose petals from the entrance to the bed where the staff made a heart out red rose petals. This was a great detail, since it was our anniversary. Thanks Valeria!!!!
The place was clean and the staff made sure our room was cleaned and kept dust free and sand free. 

Make sure you communicate all of your choices to your concierge as soon as you get there. This will assure you get into all the restaurants you want to visit for dinner and the concierge will help you book tours if you want, as well.
Our concierge, Valeria Galvez, was EXCELLENT!!! She was professional and knowledgeable. She made all our reservations to the various restaurants and we did not have to worry about anything.  If you are a member of Club Melia, which we are, there was an opportunity to upgrade. Usually my wife and I are put off by this sale pitch and shy away from them when we travel. However, Valeria was respectful and not pushy. She provided the right amount of information and backed up when we said “no”. Thank you for that Valeria. However, because of all the information she offered, we found out additional information about our membership and will be upgrading eventually. 

The food was INCREDIBLE and there was a great variety. We had many choices and the restaurants were great. We missed out on Vento but will go next time. This is extra but worht the money. The service was above and beyond at all the restaurants and bars. The staff was attentive but not over bearing. They were friendly and always responsive. Carlos, one of the bartenders at the Avenue Bar, was fantastic. They make great drinks. We had a choice as members to get the all-inclusive, which we did. Believe me, it was the right choice you will not regret it. At the buffet there was never a line and we had many choices. 
If you do not make reservations for the restaurants, check with them around dinner time and they may be able to get you in. If you do not have a concierge, make sure to go to guest services by 9am to make reservations.  I think that works best.

We did many of the tourist stuff on our own and it was very inexpensive to do. We saved hundreds of dollars. We took the camion (bus), which stops right in front of the hotel to Isla Mujeres and then the ferry. We spent the day there. Highly recommend this outing. It was easy to get to and safe. We did snorkeling. We went to Playa del Carmen, again took the camion and the ADO bus, we spent the day and it was beautiful. We went to the ciudad (city) Mercado 28 and felt safe. This was our way to be with the locals. We visited La Isla, a huge shopping mall, if you are into that with great prices. If you want to rent a car there is car rental not to far from the hotel.

If you want to just do nothing, you can do that as well at the hotel because you will not be bored. The property offered a number of activities free of charge. Check out the non-motorize aquatic activities offered by the hotel. They're right across the street at AquaWorld. 
The WiFi was fantastic we had services everywhere on the property even by the beach.

reviews.author: Ourcrew2014
reviews.title: Luxury vacation with impeccable service
reviews.text: My husband and I stayed at the Paradisus Cancun from Dec 27-Jan 3rd along with our 17 year old son. The hotel/resort is stunning and the attention to service is second to none. All of the staff were always friendly and greeting us. We stayed at the Royal Service side and highly recommend this to guests without young children. We enjoyed the private pool and our butler, Cesar. Cesar was available at our request for anything we wanted such as reserving cabanas by the pool or beach, restaurant reservations, etc. He surprised us with chocolate covered strawberries once we arrived and a bottle of champagne on New Year's Eve. Our favourite restaurant was the American Grill which is a Brazilian restaurant. The wait staff there are amazing and the food is great. Roger and Francisco, poolside waiters, were fabulous. We laughed and joked with them the entire trip and they personalized their attention to our needs. Omar at poolside was wonderful and assisted us with whatever we needed. We went to the spa many times for heavenly 80 minute massages which were some of the best we've had. The beach was beautiful and the rolling waves with the turquoise water was what you see in brochures. We have stayed at other five star resorts in Cancun and the Mayan Riviera but this resort far surpasses the others. We are already planning our next trip back. A huge thank you to our Paradisus friends - Cesar, Roger, Francisco and Omar...until next time! Michelle, Jeremy & Nicholas

reviews.author: RMY_13
reviews.title: Fabulous get away
reviews.text:
My family stayed at the Paradisus  Resort Cancun from Dec. 13 to Dec. 20. The many positive reviews played a factor in our choice. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay here.From the first time you enter the hotel lobby and see the huge atrium with a restaurant nestled among a garden area complete with a meandering fish pond, you know you are in for a special stay. As previous reviewers have mentioned, it is a huge resort with 5 interconnecting pyramids, but it is immaculately clean and sparkling.
We stayed in an ocean view suite. It was simply but tastefully decorated .There  were no issues with cleanliness. The a/c worked fine. The complimentary  in room safe was large enough to fit a laptop. An iron and board was provided, and the large closet came with 10 hangers. The shower had a rainshower head. This was the first time I had used this, and while the water pressure wasn't pounding, it was okay. The hot water would never reach scalding temperature, but it was warm enough.
 There are a variety of restaurants,  but we ate at the buffet mostly. We enjoyed our meals there. We did go to the Japanese restaurant, and thoroughly enjoyed it. The pools  were well maintained and as a result the water was crystal clear. There is a large beach area on the property, and everyone knows about Cancun's soft sand beaches and  warm waters. Most of the beach front hotels work diligently to  gather the seaweed off the beaches. It is a losing battle, but they do their best.
While we have a university aged daughter, I think the children's club the hotel provides, must be good. I saw a lot of families with pre-school age children. 
That being said, there is a special section of the hotel for adults ( 18 years and older). they have their own pool and restaurant.
All in all, we would have no problems recommending this hotel to anyone.

reviews.author: Nick T
reviews.title: Great place to completely relax.
reviews.text: Flew in to Cancun and we were picked up by the hotel service. Upon arrival we were greeted with wet towels and smiles. Towels are for your face to wipe the sweat off. Very pretty inside with hanging vines from the fifth floor and opening view to the sandy beach and blue green waters. Service is Great and the restaurants are pretty exquisite. One thing that we disliked was the sushi, Which took for ever to get and seemed like the rice came out of a burrito. close to the city if you'd wish to visit the local life. The hotel has many expeditions and Parks you can go to and experience the jungle and snorkel with fish. Xel-Ha was our spot for a waterpark which I loved. Bring bread to feed the fish when you snorkel, they will swarm you. On this last note, this is a Great spot to recharge,recuperate, revitalize.

reviews.author: Lisa C
reviews.title: Wonderful, relaxing week with kids
reviews.text:
We just returned from a Christmas week stay at this resort, with our three boys aged 12, 8 and 5.  We had Family Concierge connecting ocean view rooms.  Rooms were modern, spacious and comfortable.  Our air conditioning wasn't working the first night but it was fixed very promptly and they checked repeatedly to make sure it was fixed to our satisfaction.  The service overall was excellent.  Our butler Fernanda was gracious and helpful in making dinner reservations and ensuring we had what we needed.  

The kids pool area was beautiful - clean, gorgeous tile mosaic, wonderful waiters constantly offering drinks.  The only annoying thing was that there weren't enough chaise lounges to go around and people would go out at 6 or 7 am to reserve them.  If I went back, I would probably reserve a poolside "bed" to avoid the lounge chair rat race.  

We enjoyed the food overall.  Ate most of our meals at the Naos buffet.  Breakfast was great, especially the made to order omelets and fruit.  Lunch was awesome at La Perla outdoor seafood buffet (with the poolside buffet nearby for kids to have hot dogs, burgers, etc).  Dinner was a bit more hit or miss.  I'd say it was a step below the Club Med Punta Cana buffet in terms of quality.  Also, there were never enough waiters to clear your plate and bring drinks in a timely fashion.  A la carte restaurants were also just okay, with the best being Vento, the mediterranean tapas-style restaurant.  We fed the kids room service dinners a few time which was decent, though our special requests were never honored (such as serving the hamburger plain instead of with cheese, bacon, etc).  Everything always came exactly as described on the menu, not as we requested.  But the quality was still good and the service was fast.  

The Family Concierge lounge was super nice.  Check in and check out were so convenient and relaxing there!  Also loved the premium bar drinks, snacks and candy for the kids.  We also liked the game room there with pool table and xbox.  

We never dropped off our kids at the Kids Zone, but they did participate in some of the poolside arts and crafts.  The ladies who worked there seemed very sweet, even when some kids were bratty.  

Great free wifi throughout the resort, including poolside.  Nice for keeping in touch and posting on facebook.

My one suggestion for this resort is to add some additional outdoor options at night.  The weather and view were so beautiful, but there was nowhere to sit and eat or have a drink after dark.  And it was surprising that the pools closed at 7 pm.  We would have enjoyed a late night swim.  Another nice amenity would a a hot tub.

reviews.author: Brooklynite_Abroad
reviews.title: Now a Paradisus, but the same old Gran Melia it always was
reviews.text:
The setting:  This is the former Gran Melia Cancun, recently rebranded as Paradisus Cancun.  If you have stayed at other Paradisus resorts, you will be quite disappointed.  I stay at this property every couple of years and there wasn’t a single discernable difference about this property from a few years ago to its current reincarnation as a Paradisus.  The lobby is spacious and impressive, although dated.  The rooms are standard issue.
The room:  We stayed at a Royal Service room, which appears as any other room at the hotel.  The only difference is that there won’t be any children staying in the Royal Service pyramid, which is the north most of the five pyramids in the hotel.  The only advantage to Royal Service is the adults only pool which is located where the Level beach was.  We stayed here at the end of September and the Royal Service beach was packed.  Finding a bali bed/palapa with a nice view of the beach was impossible.  The super discounted rates for Royal Service (@$200/night vs the usual @$1000/night at other true Paradisus resorts) meant that this property was packed even during the off peak season.  The butler service, which comes with Royal Service was subpar as well; ours fully forgot to reserve our bali beds.
The food:  The breakfast buffet is the sole decent offering at this property.  The Mexican restaurants are decent but definitely skip the Asian and continental options.  This is a shame as Cancun has great restaurants so the chefs do not have to approximate other cuisines, they can try quality Asian and continental food outside of the hotel and recreate the flavors.  The mandatory all inclusive at this rebranded Paradisus is a major negative, as I would have rather paid less for the room and enjoyed the dining options outside of the hotel.
All in all, I found this property to be a solid choice when it was a Gran Melia.  As a mandatory all inclusive Paradisus, it just doesn’t hit the product quality that I have experienced and have to expect from a Paradisus.  I hope the Melia chain truly upgrades this hotel.  My biggest gripe is the need to fight for a bali bed; that should never happen at a Paradisus, especially when there was never a lack of these at the Level, during Gran Melia times.

reviews.author: k h
reviews.title: What a disappointment!
reviews.text: If you don't mind sub-par service, and poor food at an expensive price point, then this vacation is for you.  They put the "fun" in dysfunctional.  Cancun is beautiful.  The property itself is not bad.  But it lacks from any direction.  Lines, Lines, and more lines!  Book elsewhere.

reviews.author: Philip B
reviews.title: Among the best of the all-inclusives
reviews.text:
Facilities were nice -- rooms were above average, perhaps not extraordinary. The oceanview balcony was the best part of the room and had fantastic sunrise views.

The pool was excellent. Our family had several small children and the children's pool area was perfect. Be sure to go at the beginning of your stay and rent a cabana for each day -- chaise lounges are fiercely contested and defended. We also rented a beach cabana one day; beware that they're very close to loud music courtesy of a beach DJ (and occasionally, musicians).

Perhaps the best attribute of Paradisus is the quality and quantity of food & drink. Bars could make pretty much every drink imaginable using quality liquors, and the food was better than any all-inclusive I've ever visited before.

reviews.author: surfpuravida
reviews.title: Outstanding Service plus some
reviews.text: Where do I begin, OUTSTANDING SERVICE!!!! We spent the week of New years and had an amazing time. We had an ocean view room with family concierge service. We had an outstanding butler his name is Charly. CHARLY was always there like a genie in a lamp always smiling and eager to serve very sincere. The rest of the the family concierge Fernando, Andrea, Salvador, and Oscar again always smiling and super helpful. Also the Manager Reyes who made our leaving so smooth, getting our transportation and back to airport on time was very much appreciated. The other manager Veronica also very helpful and sincere. Darwin the waiter by the Koi pond always smiling and great service. We where a family of fourteen, we felt like we were the only ones there. Also Francis took care of our little one as if was here own, We highly Recommend this place, we will be back for sure!

reviews.author: Ishaan12
reviews.title: Great resort for kids and adults.
reviews.text: We came with 3 famalies to the resort. Everybody was satisfied. The food was great and with the family concierge service food was inclucive. The pool was a great way to spend the day. There are cabanas to rent and a bar. The rooms were surprisingly big. We booked a standard room. Everything about the resort was great.
