The staff was super friendly and accommodating and I appreciate the efforts of the very hard working staff in the restaurants and pool areas.
You indeed do need to be up early to reserve a beach umbrella and chairs. I would say by 6:30 to place your towels and books and then go get your breakfast and come back. Or in Royal Service you can reserve a Bali Bed around the pool and we did that for our two full days. There was no additional charge and we had no issue lying around eating guacamole and fruit and having a cocktail delivered to us.  There always seemed to be open lounge chairs around too. You could also go to the next pool over from Royal Service which is right there and it's quiet and has loungers. The main pool has a swim up bar and some more action. It was kind of like when you go visit a big city and check out the excitement and then your glad to get home to your quiet suburb in Royal Service.
Make your dinner reservations when you get there so you're guaranteed the times and places that you want. 
The food is your basic Mexico, All Inclusive fare. For us, we can always find plenty of things to love. In the real world I'm a bit of a foody.... but I get it when I'm away... Mexico is not a food destination...so find what you like and enjoy it. I for one am sure I gained a few pounds! 
Anyway... Don't worry about this hotel. the location, staff, ambiance are all fantastic! 
And for me.... there is nothing like that gem stone colored sea!!! It's what brings me back over and over!!!! 
Have fun!

reviews.author: Kate M
reviews.title: Wonderful family vacation in paradise!
reviews.text:
We are part of the Paradisus vacation club (time share) so we spent a week at Paradisus Cancun during March. This all-inclusive hotel is fantastic for those who are looking for great food, great service, and beautiful facilities. The beach is one of the prettiest I have seen and it is well-maintained. Our family included two younger children and four adults, all of who enjoyed our week in the sun.

There are many restaurants that are very good. The buffet for breakfast was always great. Their french toast was fantastic and their omlette station was always great. Lunch could either be taken by the pool with wings, fries, burgers and nachos or at two different restaurants- the buffet or the pasta/pizza/sandwiches. The wings and fries were always our favorite. For dinner, we ate at a different restaurant every night. My favorite was the sushi place but there was also a brazillian steak house, tapas, tacos, authentic Mexican, the buffet, or an adults only place (we didn't eat there). If there was ever a problem, the staff worked dilegently to correct the situation, often going overboard to make it up.  The pool was wonderful and the pool staff was very attentive- our cups never went dry.

There were a few minor issues that overall did not affect our vacation. They recently transitioned from a resort hotel to the all-inclusive Paradisus resort. There were a few cliches with the system and a bit of a language barrier since we were not proficient in Spanish, which sometimes led to difficulties with services but overall, this was a great vacation. 

As a parting thought, if you need a massage or any type of spa service, the Yhi spa at the hotel is wonderful. We got three massages and a manicure and everyone was satisfied. I am still relaxed from my massage.

Would go back in a heartbeat!

reviews.author: GreatFalls-Traveler
reviews.title: Now that was great!
reviews.text: I do not usually like to go to all inclusive resorts but this was fantastic. We booked through Cheap Caribbean Vacations and received a great deal. When we drove up to the property I was very, very impressed with the structure. When we walked in we were sent to the Family Concierge where the great staff, Fernanda in particular, took care of everything. Could not be nicer or more helpful. The Hanging gardens in the center of the hotel were amazing. The food in each of the Hotel restaurants were high quality and excellent. I really liked the hotel, the restaurants, the bars and the room. Just great. I could not have been happier.

reviews.author: Theresa1415
reviews.title: Anniversary vacation
reviews.text: Friendly and Excellent service throughout our stay in pyramid 5 (royal service).  Staff went out of their way to make this an unforgettable vacation. Manager, Lazarro Ascencio, was very helpful and immediately addressed issues.  Pool concierge, Sergio, went out of his way to ensure we are happy. He even helped to arrange a bouquet of red roses and special breakfast in the wedding "chapel" on the beach!!! Octavio, one of the servers, arranged a special desert and birthday cocktail for my birthday. We received excellent service at this resort. There are multiple a la carte restaurants and the food was excellent!!

reviews.author: Jasmolicious
reviews.title: Great Stay
reviews.text:
A belated review: 

- Stayed here last May. A gorgeous, beautiful, & luxurious resort.  Stunning, inviting, classy atmosphere. Especially loved the low volume lounge music inside the hotel. Great food, lots of selection, different each meal, 4 beautiful a la carte, excellent concierge and hotel service. Everyone had smiles on their faces, always trying to be helpful. Always felt treated like a king. Enjoyed the hotel lounge bar; each night, they had different lounge music (jazz, classic, Mexican, 80's pop), beautiful people hanging around, enjoyed conversations, drinks, and music.  
Had an all inclusive deal, mini bar replenished daily, room cleaned 2-3 times a day, clean +++ (I am a little clean freak). 

- Gorgeous powder white sand beach, absolutely no vendors, warm ocean water. What can I say more?

- Well maintained, beautiful pools, pool side activities, and chill music. 

- Overall, I could have purchased a time-share here. Though I was not asked once during my stay. It was a pricey trip for 5 nights, but really enjoyed it, definitely worth it. I want to go back there again.

reviews.author: saminnewyork
reviews.title: Pros and Cons
reviews.text:
Trip: March 21st – March 29th
We decided to take this last minute family trip to Paradisus in Cancun since our college kids came home early, two adults plus three kids 21, 18 and 12.  This review is more factual points of pros and cons, rather than grievances.
Airport - first, when you get off the plane and head out past customs, DO NOT STOP !! go straight out through the sliding doors and proceed to go outside as quickly as you can. Do not stop to talk to any of the gray uniformed personnel flanking the exit to your right and left, they are TIME SHARE reps who will waste your time. They will try aggressive tactics such as : “Please follow me, it is my job to assist you”. Answer aggressively back “No thank you” and walk past them. Can’t believe I fell for it (they wasted ten minutes of our time before I realized what they were up to and gingerly left the area). Head out, look for your transportation representative (Apple – flowered shirts , Olympus tours – Orange shirts , GoGo – light blue shirts)  and they will take care of your party.

 The resort is very beautiful, with lush green plants and trees everywhere, kept immaculately clean by an ever present maintenance staff and because it was previously a non-all-inclusive hotel, the interior design is upscale but the logistics is definitely off and I’ll explain in a minute. The beach is exceptionally clean, sand is fine and the waters are gorgeous turquoise in hue. We’ve been going to all-inclusive resorts for the past twelve years so this is not our first time. Paradisus has recently been converted to an all-inclusive establishment and we learned that this is their first year in that capacity so for effort I would give them a solid 9/10, they do however need to improve a few issues.
Rooms:  the hotel is comprised of five pyramids, number three being the main building where the restaurants, club, lounges and bars are. I believe pyramids one and five are reserved for local folks who vacation and the inner pyramids are for tourists. 
Our reservation indicated a junior suite ocean view, but when we got there, we realized that their idea of a junior suite is two rooms adjacent to one another (not necessarily connecting) and even the connecting rooms available in the entire pyramid are very few and those are given on a first comes basis.  Our rooms were situated in pyramid three; rooms 3363 and 3364 with a beautiful ocean view. The housekeeping staff arrives nightly for a turn down service, offers complimentary plates of hors dourves and chocolates – really nice touch.
Housekeeping starts cleaning rooms at around 11:00 am and many times we would come back to the rooms at around 5:00 pm from the beach, and the staff would be so far away down the hall that any chance of getting our rooms fixed was slim. We ended up just asking them to come the next day and requesting fresh towels. Talking to other guests, we discovered that the housekeeping staff does it all the time to avoid cleaning all the rooms daily. 

Let me interject here and say from experience, that all places we visited outside the states had issues with punctuality, quality of service and attention to efficiency and a friend of mine said something rather true to me: when leaving the states, lower your expectations. 
Family concierge – we didn’t use but we heard other guests were very pleased with the service and you can rent cabanas for as low as $25 a day!
Food -   The place is definitely not ready as an all-inclusive resort. The dining hall has exactly 15 (we counted) indoor tables and on a hot muggy day, you will have to wait in line to sit in the air conditioned room. Outdoor ocean view seating is available but we just sat there sweating like pigs.
Sometimes, they decide to open the Fuego restaurant or the Vento restaurant (which are closely connected to the main dining room) for guests who have nowhere to sit but it’s at the discretion of the managers. Do not expect anything to open or start at the designated time. Immediately add another hour to any indicated time.  The breakfast buffet does not open at six, because by the time the staff sashays in at 6:30 and prepares everything, the place opens close to 7:00. If you have an excursion scheduled and is pressed for time, make sure you bring the issue to Francisco, the restaurant manager, and he will do his best to rectify the problem. ( I must say that the entire managerial staff is terrific and really tries to make sure all the guests are happy). In conclusion, the buffet room is tiny, food is okay, depends how picky you are.
Fuego restaurant – we loved it, it was exceptional Latin fusion cuisine and the service was impeccable.
Vento restaurant – It is Tapas bar and as you know the portions are small but they allow you to order 4 of each item per table.  Our reservation was for 6:00 pm, the food came out of the kitchen so slowly and so far in between, that the small portions were not enough for any of us so by 7:30 we just left and walked into the buffet to eat dinner.
Moles- Traditional Mexican cuisine – I thought the food was delicious, the onion buns and whipped cheeses were fresh and seasoned, I ordered the grouper and it was really well cooked, they accommodated my daughter who’s a vegetarian but my family didn’t think the food was anything special.
We didn’t try the Japanese, the Market Grill, Tempo or Blue Agave 
Pools-  Get your pool towels as soon as you get your rooms upon check in, by 5:00 pm the fresh ones are usually all gone.  Depending whether the hotel is at full capacity, you might have to go early in the morning (those who are seasoned all-inclusive travelers will know this already) and save yourselves chairs/palapas. Some people tip the outdoor maintenance staff and they put their towels and books on their desired chairs for them at 6:00 am. We are early risers so we did it ourselves. Pool bar does not open at 10:00 am, and the ice is brought in only at 11:00 am so take water with you from the mini-bar in your room.

Entertainment:  I must admit that the shows (if you can call them that) are more geared toward kids rather than adults (can’t believe I’m saying that but I missed the cheesy nightly shows we typically have in all inclusive resorts). The hotel does not have a huge theater to accommodate all the guests so the performers present their show at the “Avenue Bar” which is located across from the Japanese restaurant. The place is small and as I mentioned, there’s not enough room for people to sit/stand and watch the show so every evening there are arguments and fights – not cool. The bar has sprawling lounge beds, couches, little corners to sit and have a quiet drink and absolutely magnificent view of the ocean and pools. 
Word to the wise – alcohol in all hotels are typically watered down (we saw staff pouring water into liquor bottles!) but this time it was watered down so much that after five tequila shots I was able to walk back to my room when typically one glass or white zinfandel takes me out!
Daily activities – Very disappointing.  They do have a large wooden board right next to the main pool indicating daily activities at different times but no one is there on time and consequently the activities never happen. Since the don’t have an actual entertainment staff,  no games are organized like bingo, fun games for the kids in the afternoon like water balloon toss, dance competitions or morning exercise on the pool deck like other resorts have.

Kids clubs:   when the weather turns gray and rainy, parents opt to send their kids to the lower level of the main pyramid (the Lanzarote room) they have a huge room for kids (it looked to me ages 3-10 but I’m not sure) with inflatable rides, games and couches. A staff of 4-6 is constantly there to supervise and parents are welcome to come in and spend time there with the kids. Teen club in the nearby room is equipped with wii, Xbox and a pool table, plus a tv comfy chairs and a dvd player.  

Prices : Can’t tell you how outraged I was to realize that most places in Cancun try to rip you off and I’m not being sarcastic. I’m well aware that tourists are easy prey and the islands are notorious for overcharging, but $40 for sunscreen at the hotel boutique is criminal. Spa services are no better, basic massage starts at $200 and I bought three bananas with two Evian water bottles, they charged me $14 at the Airport – seething as I type this.

I was going to upload pictures but the traveller’s gallery here is truly sufficient and captures the entire hotel from every angle. 
Enjoy your trip, folks!

reviews.author: Jake M
reviews.title: Family Concierge Lovers!
reviews.text:
We are kind of picky family let me say...
so we make the reservation for Family Concierge that was "one of the 2 vip areas from the hotel"...on this areaFamily Concierge, they do everything for us! they make our vacation something out of this world! it was our firts trip as a Family i have 1 kids, all the night they send to us milk and cookies, we have included like some kind of "wáter ritual" it  was awesome only if you are staying at Family Concierge, also they make reservation for the nicest cabanas by the pool área, we felt like famous, because every day our name was on the cabana...its awesome!...we definitly love Paradisus and Family Concierge, me and my family want to thank some of the Staff of Family Concierge... Isaac our personal buttler he es very funny and always take care of everything Fernanda our Concierge, she is so sweet and my kid love her, every morning she gave us a cute smile , also when she was with another person, she takes the time to make time for us...also they work to makes us a dinner reservation for Fuego that WOOOW latin fussion ufff the BEST! thanks also to all the Staff of the Restaurants they make the hard work in this hotel! food and beverage are a 10!....Thank you Paradisus and Family Concierge for everything! we dont have the Word to explain the awesome hard workers you are..

reviews.author: rustravelgirl
reviews.title: Nice stay
reviews.text:
Very nice resort, higher end than usual all-inclusives in Mexico, in food and accomodation. Lush vegetation in the lobby make you feel like you are in an exotic place.
Good food in the buffet, but check our sushi and Mexican restaurants, both are good.
Vacationed with a 1.5 year old, found it easy to walk around with a stroller, was accomodated in restaurants. Kiddie pool area is nice, some animation for the children was available.
All in all nice low key stay, but weather could have been better, but this was off season, so not too surprising.
Spa is nice as well, and the bus picks up right in front of the hotel if want to go shopping to town.

reviews.author: Yael154943
reviews.title: Great resort! Real Paradise
reviews.text:
We're just back from a week at the Paradisus Cancun. Overall it was a great stay! The pros: the food is wonderful with a lot of variety and healthy choices as well. The people who work there are all soooooooooooo nice, polite and professional! At Bana, we were served by Sandra who really went the extra mile to make us feel special! We booked the Royal Service so we had "our pool and Bali beds" Awesome!
The cons: we had some problems with our washroom and a bad smell in the washroom; we had to call express service a few times regarding that issue. We were told we would have access to a butler: we never saw him or her!!!! Sunscreen is free if you have the Royal Service, however, there is never enough of it because people are keeping it, I guess. What i suggest is that they do the same as what they do at the Trump Hotel in Honolulu: they pour some sunscreen in little containers which people can keep or / and refill. 
Some rooms are super old and not well maintained (Tower 1). We asked to change room after one day.
Overall it was a great relaxing stay!

reviews.author: Regina M
reviews.title: A real paradise
reviews.text:
I went with a few friends to Cancun in March 2013 and stayed at H. Paradisus. It was the perfect choice; the hotel is amazing. Since the very first moment, you feel like in another world of peace and happiness. The first thing that stroke me once you enter was the nice smell. Then, the lobby is like a nice forest with plants, water, ... it's very relaxing. 

You can find a variety of restaurants; with excellent food and service. The employees are very nice and professional; they are there when you need them but not on top of you all the time (as you find in the US hotels).  It was specially nice the service at the swimming pool and beach area -where we spent most of our time! Overall, the service was excellent and the common areas are really enjoyable. The rooms are amazing as well but we did not spent much time in it because there were so many things we wanted to enjoy in the common areas, the spa, as well as the beach, that we did not have time! -)

We knew the hotel was good but it certainly exceeded our expectations. I highly recommend it if you go to Cancun!

reviews.author: SR_BR_NY
reviews.title: Great location and beach, BUT!
reviews.text:
Beautiful lobby. Long wait to finally get your room. Be carefull! When you book a so called suite, it will be a regular room. For the price to stay here you have no walk in shower. Only tubs. Ridiculous! Every bathroom has lime deposits and hard water stains on all bathroom fixtures yet they keep the resort clean. Most people are very friendly but some are not.
Christian, of guest services and Max, head of food dept. made my stay much better. We had issues booking dinner reservations and some restaurants they plain suck! These two people made it a better experience and deserve credit. 
Fabulous weather every day. Easy to get everywhere and the buses comes often.
Don't buy pesos in the hotel. They will rip you off. Exchange downtown. Also, don't buy more than you need. If you exchange back to US dollars you get screwd!

reviews.author: NadiaWood
reviews.title: 2010 Global Incentive Trip
reviews.text:
I stayed at the Gran Melia Paradisus Cancun for a total of 4 nights in October 2010 whilst travelling with 200 delegates from Europe. We were attending a Global Incentive Trip in Riviera Maya for 3 days, however due to varying flight times to and from Europe we needed an alternative place to stay near to the airport for our travellers. 

We stayed on a bed and breakfast basis and I was upgraded to one of the suites which had a stunning view of the ocean. The hotel reception team were helpful and efficient at checking the group in, however concierge took some time delivering our bags (probably due to the volume of luggage!) 

The suite had a beautiful lounge area and king sized bed opening up to a balcony overlooking the pool area & with a sea view. The breakfast and hotel restaurants served a good selection of food, and there were a number of nearby restaurants too. There are some lovely little tourist shops within the hotel, perfect for purchasing gifts to take home! 

Overall we had a fabulous stay and would definitely recommend this hotel to both business and personal travellers. The passing hurricane didn't even ruin our time there!

reviews.author: Nermina B
reviews.title: Amazing Honeymoon & Perfect Resort
reviews.text: In June 2010 my husband and I went on our honeymoon to Cancun, Mexico and we stayed at Paradisus Cancun (Formerly known as Gran Melia). I have to say the resort was beyond amazing, it definitely exceeded our expectations. The pictures were really nice and we were afraid that when we get there it wouldn't look anything like the pictures. Well we were wrong, it was much better then the pictures showed, the scenery was beautiful, the rooms, and lobby area looked above and beyond amazing. I was completely thrilled, we loved the food, we usually ate at the buffet, the staff was wonderful, room service was very good, and everything about this trip and resort was just PERFECT. I would definitely recommend this resort to everyone, less than a year after I got married my sister-in-law and brother went to the same resort for their honeymoon and they loved it just as much as we did. Now it has changed, it includes a children's play area, and it looks a bit different but I am sure its just as amazing. I recently booked a trip with my husband and our 16 month old daughter and we are going to Riu Caribe in Cancun and if I had known that Gran Melia had updated to a kid friendly resort as well I would have definitely booked our family vacation there. But, you never know I might look into it once second family vacation comes around :) ( I had to choose that we traveled in June 2012 because that was the only option but we actually traveled there in June 2010)

reviews.author: Caitlin B
reviews.title: Wonderful Experience
reviews.text: My boyfriend and I stayed here for seven nights in January.  The hotel was absolutely beautiful and surpassed any of the pictures that were shown online.  The restaurants located within the facility were great; small portions, but high quality.  The rooms are very nice, and the beach area and pools were exceptional with plenty of room and chairs for all guests.  We had a great time at the pool bar! The staff was exceptionally kind and personable.  One front desk worker, Betsy, went above and beyond to make sure we had a great experience.  I would definitely recommend this resort and am looking forward to planning a trip back in the future!

reviews.author: Suzanneadinolfi
reviews.title: Awesome Hotel for honeymooners and families loved the Family Concierge
reviews.text: We stayed her for 5 nights in a 1 bedroom family concierge suite. We had a few minor problems- but everything was always handled quickly and efficiently. Fernanda, the manager for the Family Concierge, was wonderful. Honestly, all of the staff was wonderful. We never leave our child at a kids club when on vacation, but this time we did leave him for about an hour to have dinner alone. We saw how wonderful the staff was to all of the kids and felt very comfortable. The family concierge always made our dinner reservations, and we especially enjoyed Fuego. The night my husband and I had dinner at the Japanese restaurant, we ordered room service for our son, which was included free of charge. We really enjoyed the bali beds and the beach was huge with plenty of chairs and shade. The food was very good and they were always happy to make something for my picky son if we didn't see anything that he liked. This hotel had the best kids menu out of any hotel I've ever been to in Mexico. The pool is beautiful and huge, with food and drink service all day. If you are a couple without children, I went over to the Royal Service side and it is truly beautiful, especially the adults only area with bali beds. There are many adults only restaurants but also plenty of restaurants if you are traveling with children. We stayed beachside on the ground floor and it was very quiet and peaceful. The hotel is much more beautiful than it looks in the pictures, and the specialty restaurants are decorated very nicely. This was by far the best hotel I've ever been to in my 7 trips to Cancun, we will definitely come back again next year.

reviews.author: Tyler R
reviews.title: Fantastic Week of Relaxation
reviews.text: My wife and I looked at probably 200 resorts throughout the Caribbean, and the Royal Service option was what really sold us on this one. We were not disappointed. It is absolutely worth the extra $$$! The exclusive pool, bar & grill, and reserved bali beds got us away from the noise that accompanies children and college kids on spring break(which we are...just a little older). The rooms were nice enough for us, but I could see some people thinking they are not luxurious enough. Definitely get the Ocean View room and the higher floor the better. Amazing views. The food was not great, but not bad. The grounds were immaculate all throughout the resort, very impressive. The atriums were phenomenal with vines, plants, streams, and pools around every corner. We were still finding things we hadn't seen after 4 days of being there. The most impressive part of Paradisus Cancun is the staff. Absolutely incredible service from everyone we encountered. We arrived late(around 9pm) and Hector was outside helping another couple and quickly and efficiently helped us also find the separate Royal Service check-in. Hector was also our butler and although we didn't use the phone much except for dinner reservations he was more than willing to help us with whatever we needed. We asked for some mini-bottles of vodka, but we came back to our room to find .5L of Absolut. AWESOME! Julio the bartender at Palapa was fantastic every day we were there! Sergio always had our bali bed by the pool ready for us first thing in the morning and brought fruit and drinks throughout the day. Octavio, Consuela and all the other staff in the Royal Service area were also fabulous and kept a drink in our hand. We were enjoying ourselves so much relaxing by the pool and ocean that we scrapped the idea of doing anything else(main purpose of trip was to unwind). Aldo(Bana waiter) was great and offered good recommendations. You MUST go to Vento for the Mayan Coffee if nothing else.  The show that Javier put on for us while making it table side was amazing. The Red Lounge offered a quaint place to grab some late drinks and dance to a DJ's mix of music. Avenue Bar was a very comfortable spot to grab a drink and watch the little shows they put on. We didn't catch it daily, but the bits and pieces we saw looked entertaining. My wife and I will without a doubt return someday. I can only hope they continue to employ top notch employees like the few that I mentioned and everyone else that greeted us with a smile. Thanks for an INCREDIBLE week of ultimate relaxation.

reviews.author: nikkicapri
reviews.title: Spring Break 2013
reviews.text: The hotel is beautiful as well as the outside area. The rooms are spacious and nice once you figure out how to work the lights in the room and bathroom.  The tubs are high up and have an overhead shower spout as well as a handheld thing.  The buffet is a little to be desired...breakfast--no bacon or hash brown type potatoes.  It has a lot of odd type foods. Lunch - mediocore as well.  If you are not there by the time they put the food out, it becomes luke warm. They have the Market Grill ---which is pretty good (accept for the half done burgers). The best restaurant is the Asian place---not a hibachi grill. The Mexican and Med. are not what I expected. One downside to this hotel is that the club is located on the 1st floor.   You can hear the booming music throughout the hotel as well as your room.  Being on the 1st floor around the corner from the club didn't help any either.  The tequila tasting was good--Carlos Sommelser was very knowledgable on the tequila and very friendly. We had one rude waiter in the Market Grill--Rudy. He acted as if we were an inconvenience in placing orders for stuff.  Even took it upon himself to get the same drink for everyone.  When asked if he was having a bad day, he indicated that he was very busy.  The place wasn't even crowded.  The other wait staff were nice.

reviews.author: ges757
reviews.title: Return to Paradise
reviews.text:
We just returned from a wonderful family vacation! This was our second trip to this hotel only this time we exchanged our time share points so that we could also travel with our very young granddaughter and her parents. We were not disappointed. Every single person acknowledged us everywhere we went. A nice hola, or good morning does so much to make you feel good! 
We bought the all-inclusive option and were not disappointed. The food quality at all the restauraunts was just fine, we wanted for nothing. All wait staff were eager to help and quick to refill your glass. This spilled over to beach service as well, very accommodating and attentive,
There are some updates at this hotel since we last visited which added to our enjoyment.
We look forward to our return next year.

reviews.author: Karenee763
reviews.title: Lovely Hotel & Staff
reviews.text:
We stayed here for 7 nights for my 50th birthday. The hotel was lovely & the staff couldn't do enough for you. We stayed in the royal service section and felt like royalty, so much more peaceful than the main part of the hotel which was great as we travelled as a couple and wanted a nice relaxing break to recharge our batteries.
Unfortunately as I got of the plane and travelled to the hotel I had a problem with a trapped nerve in my back. The staff showed a REAL genuine concern for my welfare. They couldn't do enough for us, Erik was exceptionally helpful he even drove us to the restaurant in the golf cart & collected us after our meal so as to save me from having to walk. I had to visit the Dr on site the next morning, who was very caring & prescribed medication that the front desk arranged to collect & deliver to me all very quickly & efficiently.
All the restaurants we ate at we're lovely, but Tempo was our favourite. We ate there on my birthday and although they only had the one tasting menu it was absolutely fantastic we decided to eat there again a few nights later and enjoyed it just as much as the first time!!! We had room service every morning for breakfast, plate of fruit, cereal, toast and pastries with a large pot of lovely coffee and hot milk.
We always were able to reserve a cabana & sun beds by the pool. The beach when I was eventually able to walk again was beautiful. The sea current was very strong so I didn't venture in due to my back problem which was a shame as it looked gorgeous.
We both would recommend this hotel

reviews.author: Lesley W
reviews.title: Good Hotel and wonderful staff
reviews.text:
Have just got back from 2 weeks stay. Hotel was excellent, food very good we used the main buffet restaurant a lot very good food and lots of choice hostess Sarahi was always helpful and made us welcome. We also ate in the Bana restaurant and was served by Sandra who was very helpful and looked after us well..

The evening entertainment in the avenue bar was brilliant and again all the staff looked after us well especially Karind who had our Bar order sussed from the first day and kept us topped up on a regular basis.

All of the staff in the hotel were pleasant and helpful and the hotel and surroundings were excellent. I would definatley recomend this hotel.

reviews.author: Katherine J
reviews.title: Great resort for all ages
reviews.text: I was at Pardisius Cancun for my spring break and loved every minute of it. Besides the beautiful beaches there was always something to do. The activities staff always had something fun planned and one of the guys Diego would come and personally invite us to the activities. I think my favorite was the tequila tasting and the wine tasting but there were also fun activities at night going on at the bar. This resort has everything, theres really no need to ever leave! Overall, a high quality resort and it is even better under the new name and management. All of the staff made me feel very welcomed and I can't wait to go back again next year!

reviews.author: lindawilltravel
reviews.title: Nice place to stay
reviews.text:
We enjoyed our stay here.  We were able to upgrade to a one bedroom from a studio - it's a big upgrade.  My husband and I would drag the couch mattress to the deck and lie there looking at the stars.  No bugs so it was really relaxing.  When we upgraded we went from ocean-side to bay-side.  This was fine with me because the sun comes up ocean-side making it too glaring to hang out there in the morning, while the bay side has sunset views.  
The bed mattresses were okay but not great - it would make a big difference if they upgraded them.  The pool was fine, not as exciting as some I have seen, but rarely crowded.  The beach was very pretty.  We ate at most of the restaurants.  The Japanese one was pretty good, the others were okay.  We upgraded one night to go to Tempo.  It was FANTASTIC.  Absolutely worth it.  The meal was amazing (and I'm a foodie.)  Beautifully plated - I wish I'd had a camera to take pictures.  My only complaint is that they only have one menu - I wish they had at least two so we could have gone back.  
The resort is not all that big which I liked.  It's very easy to get around.  As others have said, it's fairly quiet.  We did a lot of day trips because there is a lot to do around there.  I would go back.

reviews.author: Trista J
reviews.title: A Good Place to Relax
reviews.text:
My husband and I were looking for a place to do absolutely nothing, aside from sunbathing and drinking cocktails.  We'd been to Cancun before but did not love it. But, when I was booking our annual trip, the Paradisus seemed to have everything at the right price. So, we gave it a shot.

Overall we were very pleased with the Paradisus. There's a lot to say, so I'll break it down by category:

Check-In/Check-Out: We did not have to wait to check-in but our room was not ready at the time promised. It wasn't too much of a problem as we had changed out of our cold-weather clothes at the airport and were able to go eat while we waited. However, when our room was ready, we were simply handed the keys and told where it was. So, we wandered around until we found it. Then, our bags never showed up even though we gave them our bag ticket and followed their directions. After 40 minutes of waiting (we couldn't go anywhere or do anything without the bags) I called to inquire. They showed-up about 5-10 minutes later without explanation as to why it took so long. It wasn't the best introduction to the hotel.  Check-out was fine. Again, we didn't have to wait.

Room: We had reserved a Lagoon View room; the room we were given was actually a first-floor room in the main pyramid with an obstructed ocean view. So, that was a nice surprise. The patio had two loungers and a small table. The room was clean and didn't have that musty, damp smell that some Mexican hotel rooms have. There was a nice couch, a couple of chairs, etc. - it was comfortable. The flatscreen TV was decent sized and a lot of channels (English, Spanish and Japanese) were available. The bathroom was fine but I did not like their toiletries - bring your own. The king-sized bed was very comfortable. The closet had a safe in it that was easy to use. We never had a problem with security. All our valuables made it home with us.  The minifridge was stocked daily with water, beer, soda, juice and snacks. We put a note in the fridge explaining that we wanted more Tecate and Diet Coke, along with a tip, so that they wouldn't leave regular Coke, Sol (the stuff we didn't want). For the rest of the week they responded to our request by filling it only we the stuff we wanted, so each day we left a little extra in there as a thank you.

Pools: There was a large pool with a swim-up bar for everyone to use. There was also a separate pool for Royal Services only. It seemed very quiet over there. Some of the Royal Service guests seemed to prefer the main pool for that reason. As with most resorts, we did need to get out there early to get a decent chair for the day. The pool is VERY cold...I guess I don't see why they would heat it but it was hard to force myself into it some days. We were able to get drinks and food (burgers, hot dogs, quesadillas, and chicken wings) without going to the bar as the servers checked-in with us frequesntly over the course of the day. My cup was rarely empty. I much preferred to deal with the pool servers as they had better attitudes and were more helpful than the pool bartenders, who I found to be the least pleasant of all the staff at the resort. There was a special area for kids that looked fun but we didn't use it as we left our son with the grandparents.

Beach: The beach was beautiful. Not all the hotels have a nice beach like this one. The red flags were up every day but people still swam. I put my feet in but that's as far as I went as the waves were a bit intimidating.  The only issue I had was with the random cigarette butts I'd find, which is more of an issue caused by the guests rather than the resort. Have some respect and put your butts in a can or something. The beach is not a giant ashtray

Restaurants: Overall the restaurants were great. The only one we really did not enjoy at all was Mole. I had some kind of turkey cutlet that had the most strange texture I've ever experienced, covered in an overly spicey sauce that had no flavor. Our favorite was probably the meal we had on our last night at Market Grill. (It's very confusing because Market Grill and Naos appear to be one restaurant, but apparently they are two separate ones. Naos is the buffet and Market Grill is outside on the deck.) One night we were eating at the buffet and the people next to us were being served giant skewers of meat - we asked if we could do that, too, but were told no, that was a different restaurant. So, the next night we made our reservations and went. It was awesome!! The food was amazing and the service there was very good. It was extra nice because it's the only outdoor restaurant - the closest you will get to dining on the beach. Fuego and Bana were also very good, too. You do need to make reservations for all of the restaurants, except for Naos. It was slightly annoying to have to stay on top of that - we didn't always know what time we were going to want to eat at on a particular night. But, if we waited until the day of we got stuck with choosing either a really early or a really late dinner time. It didn't make sense to me that reservations were required since every time we went to dinner, most of the tables around us were empty. 

Naos was the only breakfast place that we knew of - it got pretty old after the second day. The food on the buffet was often cold. They did offer made-to-order omelets if you're willing to wait in a short line. There was also a smoothie counter but I was just too lazy to get in line. There's plenty of fruit and plenty of bread to make toast, too. I liked all the varieties of juices they offered. So, my suggestion is to just steer clear of the pre-cooked stuff and stick to the items made-to-order.

If you're tired of the restaurants you can always venture out into Cancun. Every night there were shuttles taking people to off-site restaurants. I'm not sure if you need to book that in advance or how that works as we never tried it, but it's an option.

Drinks: The alcohol and beer selection was decent. They don't use crappy alcohol. For rum they had Captain Morgan, Bacardi, and a few others. For gin it was Bombay, Tanqueray, and Beefeater, etc. They'll make whatever you want. I really enjoyed the frozen strawberry daquiries, pina coladas, and mojitos with fresh mint. They had something called a mango tango that looked awesome but I never got a chance to try it.  If you're outside, they won't give you a straw, so I just kept a stash in my bag. 

Gym: We used the gym a couple of times and found it to be very nice. Everything we needed was there and I never had to wait to use a cardo machine. They have about 5 treadmills, 5 ellipticals, a couple of bikes, lots of free weights and machines.  There's a separate room where you can grab a mat to do yoga or whatever else you like. They do have group classes but I never tried one.

Activities: They don't really have any. There's a board by the pool that lists them, but they don't try very hard to recruit people so there's nothing really going on. I know this disappointed some of the more active people. I was feeling pretty lazy so it didn't bother me much.

Entertainment: I loved the nightly shows they had at the Avenue Bar, which is the indoor bar open in the evening. My favorite was probably the first one we saw on Saturday night. It was basically like a hip-hop/breakdancing show featuring many of the staff (including the guy who brought our bags to the room). I couldn't believe the skill those guys had! 

Bars: The Avenue Bar was very nice. There was a bartender there that was particularly fun but I cannot remember his name. The cocktail servers were very nice, too. There were a lot of comfortable places to sit. We never made it to the Red Lounge, which is right next to the Avenue Bar. It doesn't open until about 10, at which point we were usually in bed already (sad, I know!). I heard it was pretty lively, though, and more for the younger crowd looking to party.

Internet: The wireless was great. I was even able to use it on the beach. We never had a problem.

Renovations: They appeared to be done for the most part. However, there was a large fountain in the first pyramid next to Vento that was not operational.  It wasn't that nice to look at while dining - basically a large concrete slab with some vegetation around it. The water was out for the entire hotel one morning, which was extremely frustrating. You couldn't go to the bathroom or take a shower. Apparently they are trying to "go green" and the water issue was due to that. If they anticipated interrupted water service it would have been nice to have been told that in advance.  The morning we left, there was a lot of very loud hammering going on next to us.  All in all, though, it wasn't a huge issue and the resort does look very nice.

Tipping: Yes, it's all-inclusive but a little tipping seems to go a long way. We brought about $150 US with us and tipped when we thought it was appropriate. Some of the staff do go above and beyond, so we didn't mind thanking them for it. 

On-Site Store: They do have a convenience stoor located on the bottom level. I don't recommend counting on it, though. I ended up paying about $17 US for a small bottle of nasal spray! (There was something about this place that caused me to be very congested at night....maybe the scented candles they light at night???) But, it's there if you forget anything and are feeling too lazy to venture into town. If you do need to go into town, the bus is very convenient, cheap, and easy to use.

Other Guests: We really enjoyed the variety of people me met while staying at Paradisus. We met several people from Brazil, a couple from Argentina, and others from all over the US. 

Paradisus delivered on what we were looking for - a place to relax in the sun. I was pleased with our choice and we would probably go back next time we're feeling lazy.

reviews.author: Sabir S
reviews.title: Gran Melia to PARADISUS Cancun
reviews.text: After staying in Gran Melia Cancun in 2010, we carried the memories of the place for two year and could not resist to go again in Dec. 2012 when it became PARADISUS. It sits on a huge piece of land south of Boulevard Kukulcan for golfing. The whole resort has several buildings, offering sea and lagoon views. The central courtyard in the main building is most stunning natural beauty, plants hanging down from 8th floor to the basement level, all around with fish ponds and well designed garden with Sushi and Grill bars. White leather sofas scattered around to enjoy the central fountain. PARADISUS has undertaken extensive upgrading and additions of a dozen new restaurants. There are several pools above sea level on the south side of the buildings and very fine beach along the property line on the shores of the Caribbean Sea. Quality of food is the best you can find in all its specialty restaurants as well as the buffet place. Service staff is very friendly and obliging, will do their best to make you happy. If anyone has served you once, will remember your likes and dislikes. Over a dozen new specialty restaurants have been added. Of the old ones, we loved TEMPO by Martin Berasategui Restaurant the most (some dishes had surcharge). YHI Spa is excellent, well set between the buildings and fish ponds.

reviews.author: Bendana
reviews.title: Would go back in a heartbeat
reviews.text:
I went to the Paradisus from March 11- March 18,  2013 to celebrate my birthday. As a note, i had been looking at several hotels and worked through my travel agent Tana from Grand Turizmo travel. She is truly a very professional agent and I would recommend her to anyone. I had the pleasure to going with my husband, my sister, my brother-in-law, and three of my closest friends. Unfortunately, I rode Spirit airlines and I got to the hotel a couple of hours late. Everyone was there but me and of course I was a little irritated. We went through Lomas for our transfers and they were professional and got us to the hotel as fast as they could. I would truly recommend them. When we got to the hotel, I was in awe. The hotel is beautiful. We booked the Royal Service but did not know we're getting picked up by a golf cart. However, when we met our butler Erik, all my fears were gone. We did not wait and since it was my birthday, I requested a ocean front room and that is exactly what I got. The room was amazing. When the butler walked us up, he  offered us a bottle of spirits and gave us a full overview of the grounds and restaurants. I knew this would be a wonderful trip. I want to provide the pros and small cons of the resort.
PROS:
1. The hotel lobby is beautiful with vines, greenery, flowers, and ponds with koi fish
2. The avenue bar is just in one word- sexy.. The Bali beds, soft chairs, views of the ocean, and lighting
3. Tempo restaurant was amazing. If you stay 7 nights in the Royal Service, the 45 dollars is waived. The 8 courses, which included three deserts were amazing.
4. The staff wear amazing.. Jonathan at Vento, Enrique at Naos, And all the bartenders at the pool bars and Bana. In addition, the bell men were wonderful.
5. The resort is clean and absolutely beautiful
6. The drinks were top shelf and never watered down.. Grey Goose and Don Julio
7. The homemade smoothies at Naos
8. The ocean was beautiful and spacious
9. The spa and gym were very beautiful with an excellent sauna and steam room
10. The red lounge was fun and the DJ was willing to play whatever you want
11. The Royal service is great with the butler service. You get a cell phone and you can call from anywhere and get what you need.

CONS:
1. The breakfast at Naos was mediocre but enough food to be ok
2. The food at Naos was lukewarm
3. The lady providing currency exchange was not friendly at all
3. The pools and hot tub were very cold

Overall, this place is wonderful and I will definitely be back. I would research the negative reviews because this hotel has it all.

reviews.author: Selim B
reviews.title: Couldn't ask for more !
reviews.text: My week at the Paradisus Cancun was just Awesome ! Friendly Staff, All of them, they are always here to give you a smile !! I felt like home since my first day ! High quality service !! Delicious diverse food everyday !! Wonderful beach, I had the best time ever to relax ! I would definitely advice this place for anyone who plan to visit Cancun .. Don't miss it !!!!

reviews.author: Amy1990_11
reviews.title: AMAZING!!
reviews.text: Im a 22 year old girl who went here for 10 days with one of my best friends, we had the most amazing time at this hotel. All of the staff are friendly and welcoming wherever you go, always willing to help you. The food at the hotel was lush, something for everyone and different everyday, was worried at first as had read bad comments on here before we went about the food. We went to coco bongo when was out there, would defiantly reccommend to anyone was an amazing night out! I would defiantly reccommend this hotel to all sorts of ages, young, old, familes. This hotel was by far one of the bestest i have ever stayed in!!

reviews.author: Brenda S
reviews.title: No matter what, you will come back relaxed
reviews.text:
After staying in another Paradisus in Dominican and having a terrible experience, I set my expectations low for this one, so keep that in mind.  We got an amazing deal and were able to upgrade to Royal Service for very little - that made all the difference.  So if you are going, UPGRADE to Royal Service...you can reserve a poolside cabana every day, which is where we spent most of our time.

Pro's:  
- Most of the staff was incredibly friendly and willing to bend over backwards for you (except for our butler and one grumpy guy at the breakfast/lunch buffet)
- The staff was meticulous about keeping up the resort.  They combed the beaches every morning, cleaned out the ponds and were always working hard.
- The beach was beautiful.  
- We were upgraded to a room with two balconies with a beach view!  Cabana's were always available at the adults only bar and it was always quiet and pleasant there.
-The nightly shows at the avenue bar, the performers were fantastic!
Con's:
- No hot tub...anywhere on the resort!  We dipped our feet in every area that looked like it could be, but nothing.  It was in the upper 70's/low 80's the whole trip and very windy, so it get's pretty chilly.  The pool was waaayyy too cold to enjoy, so it was a bummer not be able to really get in the water in the day or at night!  
- No evening pool/ocean side bar. 
- A little overly trendy.  Techno music playing constantly everywhere (some of it was pleasant spa like techno, but still techno).  There was a dress code at the restaurants and you had to make reservations at all of them.

Overall, would I recommend it?  Probably.  But if I were going again, I would want to try somewhere just a little less trendy and a little more unique - but hey, it's Cancun!

reviews.author: joy m
reviews.title: Beyond Amazing....
reviews.text: This is one of many trips we have taken to Mexico, and not our first to the Paradisus Cancun (formerly Gran Melia).  My husband and I were blown away by the renovations, quality of food, new restaurant choices and of course the staff.  From the moment we arrived, our check in was seamless and our room was beautiful.  Many thanks to Maria and Yvette.  What truly makes this hotel stand out from the rest is the staff.  Rody Marco at Fuego is alway there for us.  And our dear friends Carlos Duarte and Mario Vasquez (or should I say family) work so darn hard to attend to every detail! They welcome us with open arms and offer us the best service we have had anywhere in the world. We were nervous that our favorite  restaurant  "Tempo" had changed, but once again our dear friend Ignacio and the manager Olsen took great care of us.  The tasting menu by the new Spanish chef  (Martin B.) was unbelievable!  Better than any recent meal we have had in NYC.  Service at the beach/pool was spectacular as well. And the staff at Naos and  Market Grill...Victor, we sure miss your laugh and contagious smile!  At the Market Grill you will be greated by the nicest hostess anywhere..Ayerelli.  My husband and I also had a massage at the Yhi Spa and both were the best ever.  We will count the days until our next visit, and it will be your priviledge to be guests at the Paradisus Cancun!

reviews.author: LKM1979
reviews.title: Not What It Seems
reviews.text:
I haven’t written a Trip Advisor review in quite a while, but I feel compelled to do so after staying at this resort and reading the other reviews. My husband and I stayed at the Paradisus from March 9 to 16, all-inclusive, non-Royal Service. While this resort is beautiful, I think if you carefully read the responses from the management at Paradisus to other reviewers’ comments on this site, you’ll glean all you need to know about this resort – if something is wrong, it is either a “misinterpretation” by the guest, or an “exception” that guest experienced. In summary, it’s the guest’s fault. 

The staff at Paradisus is unorganized and they simply do not care. I’m a firm believer in you get what you give – we always tip staff and make a point to be courteous to everyone, speaking Spanish when we can, etc. But, at the Paradisus, the majority of the treatment we received was condescending and bordered on disdain. Perhaps if we were Royal Service guests or with the convention we would have been treated with more respect? 

In terms of the restaurants, the buffet food was great. However, getting seated was always a hassle due to lack of tables and unorganized staff. The Market Grill, Vento and Fuego are basically connected to the buffet, so I’m not sure how those are really considered separate restaurants. There may be separate menus, but they all run together. Vento is not outside, as is described on Paradisus’ website, and it is frequently used as run-over buffet seating. 

Room service was limited, but tasty and efficient. We ate at Blue Agave (tacos) and had an average experience. Mole, next door, repurposes the food from Blue Agave. For example, chicken mole enchiladas were the chicken tacos (not kidding) from Blue Agave covered in a cold mole sauce. And, the conchinita pibil seemed remarkably similar to the carnitas we had the night before at Blue Agave. La Perla was closed to guests, except for convention parties. The bad food, coupled with the often rude service, lead us to eat at some of the great restaurants near this resort (several are within walking distance or a quick ride on the great bus system in the hotel zone). 

The gym is sub-par and seemed as though it was an afterthought. It’s in the basement with no windows, thumping club music and not enough machines. Good thing it only rained one day so we could go outside. 

Also, just a warning – if you have trouble climbing stairs you may want to consider another resort. There are several stairs up the front of the resort (to take the bus, etc.) as well as to access to pool and beach areas.

I will say that the beach and pool areas are beautiful at this resort. However, I will be staying at another resort, with another beautiful beach and pool area, next time I’m in Cancun.

reviews.author: Chris M
reviews.title: Exceeded our Expectations and Trust.
reviews.text:
Such a beautiful clean helpful friendly safe resort.

We have been all over Mexico and this was our best expierience yet. 

The entire resort was spotless. From rooms to the beaches and 24 hour room service.
.
We normally have bad experiences with hard beds in all Mexician resorts but the beds at Paradisus we like Heaven. We felt rested every morining, almost choosing staying in bed rather than getting out in the sun.

The restaurants were amazing. We went to the sushi restaurant 3 times.
Making late reservations were never a problem. The wine lists are very good and themed to each restaurant.

In the last day we lost our IPad and IPhone. We thought that we were robbed from either staff or a guest. Feeling devistated, we went to the Guest services Desk and to our surprise house keeping found our lost items and they were returned to us.

Honestly the best Mexician get away ever.

Even though we felt the pools were cold, we will go back to the Paradisus next year.

reviews.author: Roxanne A
reviews.title: 1 week stay
reviews.text: Traveled from March 3rd-9th. First I must say that this resort is breathtaking! The pictures don't do justice. My friend took me here for some much needed R&R, and I that is exactly what we found at Paradisus. The service staff was impecable. Anything you need, they are right there for you. We opted for the royal side which I must say is definately worth it. We had an amazing butler named Hector. He was so kind and polite and right there for any of our needs. We did not find it necessary to make reservations in the evenings because you can pretty much walk into any restaurant and get seated. Twice we went to Bento the sushi restauant and the hostess Victoria and our waiter Antonio were wonderful. Even though the restaurant was closing, they never tried to kick us out. They do not have a huge selection of sushi. Mostly tuna. Fair tasting. Our favorite restaurant was Vento. The food was outstanding and our waiter Jonathan was amazing! Another favorite waiter was Rogelio at La Palapa restaurant on the beach. Whenever he saw us coming, he already had our drinks ready for us to enjoy on the beach. The beach on the royal side was nice and quiet. Never too crowded which we liked. People walked around on the beach trying to sell you stuff all day, which we did get suckered into quite a bit! Got some great stuff. They are not pushy though, if you say no, they leave you alone. The pool water was pretty cold so opted to swim in the ocean everyday. It's too beautiful not to. We stayed in a 1 bedroom suite that had 2 bathrooms which is nice. A lot of the days there was a funky sewer smell coming out of the 2nd bathroom floor drain which they promptly came and fixed. Our room faced the lagoon which we loved because everyday after leaving the beach at 5:00, we got to watch the sunset from or balcony. It was beautiful. Staying at Paradisus truly makes you feel like you are in paradise!!!!!!

reviews.author: Doc58NewJersey
reviews.title: Change in name, nothing much else
reviews.text: We have been coming here (formerly Melia) for many many years.  Nothing really has changed for the better with the new high status name.  Now you do have an all-inclusive option which we prefer to not take since there are many really great local restaurants--some within walking distance; all within a quick and cheap bus ride away.  Basically our observations with new name were that 1) the rooms and amenities are virtually unchanged, 2) there were some color changes to the common area decor, 3) they expect you to wear a rather annoying bracelet identifying your all inclusive or not status, and 5) the breakfast quality took a nosedive.  That aside, the positives remained intact--great beach, friendly staff, decent fitness room (for a hotel), clean, and a good location.  If you hit a great stretch of weather (which we usually do in March) this area is truly breath-taking.  One final note, we happened to overlap with the Spring Breakers (more staying there than we had ever seen before); I am not sure if it was coincidence, but their rooms seemed sequestered in another tower (pyramid) so it was pretty quiet.

reviews.author: Kelly F
reviews.title: 2 weeks maybe too long
reviews.text:
My travel Dates :  Feb. 24,2013-March 10,2013
The hotel property and grounds are well maintained.  Pool areas and beachfront with ocean great.  There were 4 of us travelling together.  Check in went quickly but initially we didn't get the room requested.  Two of us had to fight for a room change that we were confirmed for.  Breakfast is limited to the buffet restaurant as well as lunch.  The poolside grill is not always available.  The restaurant variety is good.  8 in total.  Encouraged to do reservations for dinner.  Tempo restaurant is a charge of $45USD.  There is a late night buffet from midnight to 0400 hrs in the buffet restaurant which is poorly advertised.  Poolside activities minimal.  Nightlife at hotel quiet after the Avenue bar closes.  The disco goes until 0200 hrs and depending on the location of your room you can sing to Usher in your sleep.  The hotel shops only take pescos.  Bus service great.  Only 1USD and run every 5-10 min.  Safe to travel on.  Hotel caters to conference clients in large groups.  This hotel does not allow you to play in the Paradisus resorts in Playa de Carmen.  Not  a true Paradisus and not at all like the other Paradisus properties.  They really push the time share here.  We were approached on a daily basis to attend a session and declined.  The bartenders at the poolside bar were great especially Tona, Julio.  Wait staff were were great too.  Hats off to Mairsol, Loius, Antonio in the Avenue bar,  The deejay in the disco was great.  Poolside music needs to go or be changed.  Check out was fast.  We were in the My Time package and the guest services staff that we dealt with were not very friendly and took their time to serve you.  Overall, the trip was relaxing and had minimal stress.  The weather can be so so.  Bring a sweatshirt as can get cool at night.

reviews.author: GENE C
reviews.title: CLUB MEMBER OF THE GRAND MELIA (PARADISUS)
reviews.text:
THE PARADISUS CANCUN (THE OLD GRAND MELIA) What a beauiful place with awesome service.  We were greeted by Gaby from club membership and she treated us lke her family.  She was very helpful the whole trip..  The service we received from breakfast to dinner was the best:  Ruben & Jeremias (he is soooo funny) & Alfredo & Naos waited on us most of the time, they were just the best.. The beach & pool is beauiful.... (I'll be back for sure)

GENE C.

reviews.author: dcindc2003
reviews.title: Standard all-inclusive resort
reviews.text: I stayed here with work colleagues this past weekend and overall the service was good and the food was decent.   Nothing special here but it is a quick trip to the airport and perfectly serviceable.   It is close to the downtown area, but road at night is very busy so expect the trip to take 45 minutes.

reviews.author: legendair1
reviews.title: Quiet retreat excellent accommodations
reviews.text: Quiet retreat, the accommodations are very modern did not have time to access the 'a la carte' restaurant but the buffet was only average. All the premise were very clean and staff were polite. Plenty of pools and beach surface

reviews.author: secondfloor
reviews.title: Luxe, but not Mega Posh
reviews.text:
This new all-inclusive resort has a lot to offer. There are amazing beaches, three gorgeous pools, tennis courts, organized sporting activities (soccer, volleyball, aqua-aerobics, etc), a well-equipped gym and a spa that has high-caliber treatments, a sauna, a steam room and a really cool aquatherapy element that is offered gratis to Royal Service (the highest caliber) package members, daily! Phew. And then there are the food options, of which, I think there are eight. Basically, you will find almost any kind of cuisine without leaving the premises. But make reservations early, upon arrival or you'll be eating at 11pm. And if you don't see it, ask -- they can generally rustle it up (ask for real shredded cheese on the nachos instead of cheese sauce, if there's no salmon at the breakfast buffet on the weekends, ask for it and you will receive it). 
My issue is with the Royal Service, adults-only highest caliber service offered at the resort. I don't know if everyone experiences what I did, but mine was not the stellar service experience I associate with staying at a place with butler service (like a St Regis resort). First, when I moved rooms b/c I was concerned with the safety of my first room on the ground floor, it took them over an hour to bring my suitcase. My butler offered two specific services, I agreed to take them, and then he never followed through with either. My colleagues all received things like daily newspapers, petit fours in the room, requested items in their mini-bars and I got none of this, though I asked daily. We each asked for specific toiletry items and it took at least three requests before we got them. On my last full day there, a Saturday, I left my room at 930am and when I returned at 5p, my room had not been touched -- there were still dirty dishes there from the night before. And after offering luggage pick-up, no one came for my bags. It seemed like there were a lot of cracks in the exclusive service. If I were to go again, I would perhaps pay for a lower level of service, adjust my expectations and probably be a lot happier.

reviews.author: BDL67
reviews.title: Outstanding Service
reviews.text:
Outstanding service, good food, however a few things that are annoying to take it from 5 stars to 4. 
- pool water temperature cold, ocean is warmer
- there is no place to sit outside in the evening with bar 
- sometimes difficult to get reservations at restaurants but most of the time hey were only half full

reviews.author: Beyond_YXU
reviews.title: A Very Chic Mega-Resort With Lots to Offer
reviews.text:
We stayed for one night at Paradisus Cancun at the start of our annual March Break vacation.  Our flight wasn’t arriving until 6:30pm, and we didn’t want to arrive in Playa del Carmen after dark, so I looked for something closer to the airport for that first night.  I found an awesome deal for Paradisus Cancun, so since we’d never actually stayed in Cancun proper before, we thought this would be a great opportunity to check it out.

The hotel was about a 15 minute, $35 transfer from the airport (USA Transfers).  Upon arrival the first thing that strikes you is the sheer size of the property and of the hotel itself.  We were the only people checking in, so service was friendly, efficient and prompt.  We were immediately impressed by the décor in the stunning lobby, the smartly uniformed staff, the pleasant scent and the soothing music.  There were fresh flowers and lit candles everywhere.  It’s a great night time hotel!

We were escorted from the front desk to the private check-in desk off the lobby.  Again, we were impressed by the recent renovations and redecorating since Paradisus took over the property from Melia.  Within less than 10 minutes we were checked in, given our bracelets (the most attractive all-inclusive bracelets we’ve ever been assigned), and were on our way to our sixth floor room in the main pyramid. 

The room appeared to be recently redecorated and refurnished.  While it wasn’t especially large or fancy, it was in good shape and was more than comfortable for one night’s stay.  The room overlooked the lagoon side of the resort—a pleasant view, but not as dramatic as overlooking the pools and sea.

The bed was very comfortable, and the bathroom was a decent size with marble counter, one sink, separate water closet with bidet, and tub/shower combination. The provided Clarins products included soap, shampoo, conditioner and body lotion.  Towels were a decent quality as well.  Bathrobes and slippers were not included in our room category. 

The mini bar had the usual sodas, beer and water.  24-hour room service was also included, but the menu was rather limited and we did not take advantage of it.  

We chose to dine at Bana, the Asian restaurant, since we were able to be seated immediately and we liked its situation in the central atrium with its dramatic mood lighting and lush landscaping.  We loved all the ponds (stocked with the biggest Koi you’ve ever seen), fountains and waterfalls.  Dinner was decent (sushi, sashimi, tuna, margaritas) if not particularly memorable.  Service was very pleasant.  

After dinner we walked around the property.  The other restaurants looked very attractive, all with their own distinct menus and décor.  The lobby bar was featuring live entertainment that night (hip hop dancers) and there were lots of people standing around enjoying the show.  Upon returning to our room, we were pleasantly surprised to discover that we’d been given turndown service.

The next morning we enjoyed a workout in the fitness centre (did not seem to be recently renovated but was adequate), then went for a walk along the beach to check out the nearby resorts.  Upon returning, we had breakfast at the buffet, which is a large, light-filled space with lots of options presented neatly and artistically at various stations throughout the venue.  We chose to eat outside and enjoyed the sound of the surf (which also helped to drown out some of the noise of the dozens of other guests dining at the same time).  

We noticed that by 10am all of the beach loungers and almost all of the pool loungers had already been ‘claimed’ by invisible guests with visible towels.  If we were to stay at this resort again, we would certainly upgrade to the Royal Service section to gain access to its dedicated pool (with cabanas) and beach (with more loungers and palapas).  Even by 11am, when we were about to check out, there was lots of available seating in the Royal Service area.

Overall Paradisus Cancun was a pleasant surprise.  We liked its chic, sophisticated, zen-like atmosphere.  Although Cancun in general does not hold a lot of appeal for us (too large, too congested, few palm trees), we would consider spending a few days at Paradisus again at the start or end of a trip to the Riviera Maya.

reviews.author: DItasNY
reviews.title: Change, Balance & Maximum Impact
reviews.text:
We've been coming to Cancun for 20 years because of the most hospitable people, the gorgeous beach and good food.  We've been staying at Gran Melia - now Paradisus - for 18 yrs now and staying 3 weeks minimum at a time so we see a lot and look for consistencies. Their Hanging Green Garden & Oasis Lobby immediately draws you in and takes you back to Nature, Water & Serenity. Completely unique to Melia/ Paradisus  and sets them apart from the other 4-5 star hotels (The Ritz, Secrets, Le Meridien etc).  The Koi Pond is a very special touch. Kids LOVe them!  The property is blessed with one of the widest beaches on the strip and because of the low pyramid shape of the 5 buildings, the beach gets the longest sun during the day (as the The Ritz a few doors down and sadly, on the contrary, JW Marriott's Tall bldg blocks and loses sun by around 3 pm which is a SIN considering this beautiful white powder beach & turquoise water)!!! 
SO Happy to finally get back the extra palapas on the beach since losing them to Hurricane Wilma in 2005. BIG Big plus & your responsibility to protect your guests from sunburn so they can really ENJOY their vacation and not be in pain as the past 7 yrs!!!! THANK YOU Mgmt. 
The food is good enough at Paradisus but of course there's plenty of room for improvement.  Here are the BEST to eat, 
Delish croissants for b-fast , Great Fresh Fruit Bar always & consistently, fresh fruit shakes in the morning, Fresh Eggs/Omelette station. Really appreciate the very orange yolks so you can tell totally Fresh! Bring BACK the authentic tortillas with red onions, green sauce and white cheese on top! That was one of the best dishes for bfast! WHY take it away? 
Grilled Chicken, Shrimp, Steak - can't go wrong with that . Salad Bar is very good. PLEASE always include your fresh delicious BEETS (betabel) every day for lunch & dinner. Prime Rib, Turkey, Sirloin Steak- good. Pasta Station Always a big hit.Please ADD Garlic continuously , & bacon bits, for pasta station for variety.  Carnitas Tacos at Blue Agave -Best. At VENTO restaurant, the Seranno  Ham with awesome Manchego cheese and tomato chutney on crunchy and light bruschetta - Great! Our favorite hands down. Reminds us of Spain. Should have it available for lunch and dinner all the time at NAOS too. The Creamy polenta with truffle oil is very tasty. TheBeef medallion too - at VENTO. The HOUSE Cabernet wine consistently very good at any restaurants. 
Melia/Paradisus  staff has always been very good and super friendly. Cancun in general has always been a draw for us mainly bc of its Very Warm People (Bahamas turned us off big time bc of the people. NOT at all hospitable for the most part). Jamaica- we always hear too dangerous and can't really explore outside hotel without being scared! Not good. 
OK since Melia/Paradisus has been around since the mid 80s, of course it's not as new & shiny as the newer hotels in the area. The rooms are consistently very Clean - Housekeeping works very hard at cleanliness. Well Done!  New furnishings and clean Count Most! 
The KIDS Club & Staff is very good. The girls are very warm, friendly and genuinely enjoy entertaining the little kids. Some things to consider for improvements outside Kids Club.....
Really need to build some kind of Kiddie Pool with slides (maybe off to the side where swing set is now) is a good spot. Slides are big attraction to Kids year after year. Kids prefer fun in the water versus swings. Swings they can do back home! 
Add mini Rock Climbing like Paradisus Playa del Carmen has. ADD Bocce Ball - doesn't take much space at all. 
PLEASE PLEASE TONE DOWN your club like music during bfast! Absolutely inappropriate to play Loud music that only sounds like Boom Boom Boom!!! That belongs in your Red Lounge Club , the dance clubs in town and the spring break crappy hotels like Oasis next door. Your guests are more civilized and have higher standards and expectations than that- Family with young kids are your core customers and Classy single people mostly.  For example , Please Feel free to play quality Bossa Nova music outside Market Grill especially since Brazilian BBQ is the theme at Market Grill. 
DO tone down the loud music over VENTO restaurant as well. Way too loud and people can't hear each other talk!  

Entertainment
The Best ones are the Mayan Performers on  Tuesdays  and the opera and flamenco dancer/music on Thursdays. 
The acrobats of Cirque Paris are very good too. Don't waste your budget on the in-house dancers. They're not good or entertaining at all! 
Really hope you find a good reggae band and variety pop/Latin singer/band to fill in the rest of your week. Great Music is priceless and memorable to your guests. 

Please keep up good quality of food and continue to make it better. Just see what the Ritz is serving for start and tweak and add more. 
Manage your music better all around.  It's not a Club Hotel. It's a high quality establishment. It's NOT cool at all to have senseless loud music at all times of day. Quality Relaxing and enjoyable music to everybody would be greatly appreciated and a very Classy Thing to Have. It's a MuST,  really. 

The hotel looks great with the lobby updates but please be careful not to over do it as to NOT LOSE your serenity warm authentic feel you've had all these years.

reviews.author: Sue G
reviews.title: The ups and downs of a holiday
reviews.text: We stayed at this hotel from 26th February to the 12th March. First of all a few thank you's to some great members of staff. Firstly to Gabriel and some of the team who looked after me when I was hit in the face by the backrest of my sun lounger that got caught up in the wind. Secondly to Alex and the team in the Avenue Bar. What a great bunch of guys you were. Thank you for making every evening such a good time. Thirdly to Israel and his staff in the Market Grill. You all work very hard and make the evening most enjoyable. My last thank you is to Keri and Andrea, two great American ladies, who we used to meet up with at the Avenue bar. Now, about the hotel. What a lovely place this is. We were in Pyramid 3 which is where all the shops and restaurants are. Our meeting with the Reception staff on arrival was cool to say the least. They showed no interest in us at all. We were given a sheet of paper telling us which restaurants we could eat in. This sheet did not include all the restaurants in the hotel so  we spoke to our Rep and asked why, as we were all inclusive, were we being discriminated against. He came back and told us that it had been a mistake! The only interest shown to us was with the time share people who at every opportunity will try and get you into conversation but be firm and tell them you are not interested. Our room was big, with a balcony overlooking the sea, but with no balcony furniture. Spoke to our rep and soon after two chairs were placed on the balcony. Ate in some of the specialist restaurants. Our favourite was Feugo followed by Vento. The Market Grill was good but sometimes it was just too windy to sit and enjoy the food. We had a great holiday but the weather was not always sunny which was disappointing.

reviews.author: Lou M
reviews.title: Paradisus Resort, Cancun, Mexico
reviews.text: We have good things and bad to say about Paradisus (all inclusive). Most important: This place is just beautiful. Well kept and huge. The lobby/atrium it's something that everyone should see. The staff (specially Bianca) was attentive and ready to serve you. The views, whether is ocean view or bay view is outstanding (except from the 1st floor over Naos Grill). The pools are just beautiful. The Red Lounge is excellent for drinks and dance late at night. As far as restaurants, they claim to have 8. Yes they do, but for one Naos is counted twice and two others are not availble to the "regular" all inclusive plan. We liked Naos for breakfast and lunch. La Palapa (on the pool side) is only available to convention parties. Tempo is available only to those who want to pay for their dinner. Bana (Asiatic Fusion) is smack in the midlle of the Atrium. The food is good and the atmosfere is grandiose. Mole is just a place we do not recommend. The service is good but the food is below par (if you go there do not have Taco Deco de Papas con Chorizo, stick with Costilla de Certo en Recado Negro). We did not go back there. We loved Fuego so much that we went there twice. We recommend paying extra for the lobster. The steak/filet mignon is outstanding. Lastly is Vento (which is adjacent to Naos), simply stay away. Of no fault to the resort, we just had a very cool weather (73 to 78 and always windy, beginning of March 2013) and because of that we were cold sitting on the beach and never got into the pool (neither did anyone else). But here is the most annoying item: if you wanted to get a chair/hut on the beach you would have to go down there and occupy one by no later than 8 AM, or else there would be none available (yes that is true on any day). This is something that we never experienced at any resorts we've been. Other nuisances are that we got there at 4 PM and our room was not ready (what happen to 3 PM checkin?) and one hour later they gave us the worse room in the place (the one on the first floor over the restaurant). After speaking with a manager they prepared another room for us, yet another hour later. But the second room was on the second floor overlooking the pool and ocean and it was just outstaning.
